abstract: PbS nanomaterials fiber amplifier was fabricated by coating PbS nanomaterials onto tapered fiber. PbS is deposited by atomic layer deposition technique. The influence to optical properties is discussed when changing the structure of tapered fiber.

articleTitle: Enhanced Adaptive DBP Using Extended Godard’s Error for 16-QAM Coherent Optical Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An enhanced adaptive digital backpropagation (A-DBP) scheme based on extended Godard’s error is proposed and demonstrated experimentally for 16-quadrature amplitude (16QAM) modulation formats.

articleTitle: An Optimization Scheme based on Transmitters Selection for MIMO VLC Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) visible light communication (VLC) is one of the promising solutions for future network environment. Considering in most cases, the transmitters and the receivers cannot meet the requirements of the ideal layout. This paper presents an in-depth study on the channel matrix of the MIMO visible light communication system. The singular value decomposition (SVD) is used to select the transmitters which have good performance for transmission, and the corresponding power is allocated according to the principle of equal bit error rate (BER) of the receivers. Simulation results show that this method can effectively improve the channel capacity of MIMO VLC system, and can achieve good BER performance for each receiver.

articleTitle: Optimization BM3D Algorithm Based on Pseudo-3D Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A optimization BM3D algorithm based on pseudo-3D transformation (incomplete 3D transformation) is proposed to solve the problem of huge computational of BM3D image denoising algorithm. Firstly, one-dimensional wavelet transform was carried out on the third dimension of 3D similar blocks to get one-dimensional coefficient blocks. Then the lowest-frequency coefficient block gotten above was transformed by two-dimensional transformation. Following, two-dimensional inverse transformation was performed on the lowest-frequency coefficient blocks after hard threshold filtering or Wiener filtering. And finally, one-dimensional inverse transformation was carried out on the third dimension to get the noise reduced image. The performance of the proposed optimization method is very closed to the original BM3D algorithm, but the computation of pseudo-3D transformation is only 1/3 of that of 3D transformation.

articleTitle: Design of Slot Coupled Microstrip Bandpass Filter Based on Defected Ground Structure (DGS)
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a slot-coupled microstrip line filter based on Defected Ground Structure (DGS) is designed. It is a band-pass filter. It is simulated by HFSS software. At the same time, the equivalent circuit of the designed filter is extracted by ADS software. The performance of the filter is verified by comparing the simulation results of the two filters.

articleTitle: High-linearity silicon modulator based on a reconfigurable microring-assisted Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a high-linearity silicon electro-optic modulator based on single ring-assisted Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI). The best spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of the third-order intermodulation distortion (IMD3) is 109 dB·Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup>. The linearity is comparable to the commercial lithium niobate modulators. The device can find potential applications in microwave photonic systems.

articleTitle: Fast high-resolution spectral sensing with a single frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Transmission spectra of a phase-shift fiber Bragg grating and H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> CN gas at comb-line-defined resolution of 54.5 MHz are measured within 2 μs using heterodyne detection of a broadband comb and a continuous wave laser.

articleTitle: Numerical study on a proposed photonic crystal fiber with large modal separation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We investigate the characteristics of optical modes in a new designed hollow-core photonic crystal fiber (PCF), including the large effective refractive index difference between the four vector beams and chromatic dispersion.

articleTitle: Object Wedge Angle and Direction Identification Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate identification of object wedge angle and direction using machine learning algorithms based on received beam intensity profiles. CNN outperforms other algorithms with 100% accuracy. Proposed technique reduces the complexity of hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Construction of Mach-Zehnder interferometer in no-core fiber using single straight in-fiber waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a new fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer in no-core fiber based on single straight waveguide fabricated by femtosecond laser. The device is simple in structure and fabrication and is robust, and can be used for high temperature and bend sensing, with the sensitivity of of -278.86 pm/°C and 0.28nm/m-1, respectively. Moreover, the free spectral range of the interferometer device can be easily controlled and in a precise manner.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Tuning Compensation Method for OFDR Systems Based on Polynomial Regression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A nonlinear tuning compensation method for optical frequency domain reflection systems based on polynomial regression algorithm is proposed in this paper. Simulation results demonstrate that this method has greatly improved the spatial resolution of measurement.

articleTitle: Mode Transition in Conventional Step-Index Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The discrete self-imaging effect reveals the distinct properties of cladding modes with core modes in step-index optical fibers, as was shown in our previous work [1], where only the linearly polarized LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub> modes were studied. In this paper, the dispersion diagram of the first 17 vector modes (TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub>, HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</sub> and EH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</sub>) and the related first 9 LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</sub> modes are calculated by both the full-vector finite element method and the graphical method with a three-layer step-index optical fiber model. The cladding modes distributions and the transitions between the core and cladding modes are analyzed. The results of this work are intended to enrich the knowledge and understanding of modal characteristics of conventional step-index optical fibers.

articleTitle: Germanium telluride nanosheets for ultrafast photonics
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we fabricated GeTe based optical modulator, named saturable absorbers (SAs), and utilize it in the Er-dopted fiber laser cavity for passively Q-switched and mode-locked pulse trains generation. We systemically investigated the nonlinear optical properties of GeTe-SA by OA Z-scan measurement at 800 nm and 1550 nm, respectively. GeTe-SA displays obvious saturable absorption signal with modulation depth of 16.5 % for 800 nm and 3.7% for 1550 nm, respectively. Mode-locking performance is achieved with the ultrashort pulse duration of 680 fs centered at 1562 nm. Stable Q-switched pulse trains are also observed with the maximum output power of 43.2 mW, maximum pulse energy of 315 nJ, shortest pulse duration of 0.978 μs and repetition rate ranging from 74.5-137 kHz. The results would contribute to extend the practical applications of metal monochalcogenides from nanoelectronic devices to optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Research on Nonlinear Fiber Laser with Short Brillouin Gain Fibers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Nonlinear fiber lasers with short single-mode fibers (≤100m) are investigated. The effects of the length of the Brillouin gain fiber, i.e. the single-mode fiber, and the optical filter are studied. The experimental results indicate that the fiber laser can operate well with 50m single-mode fiber if the optical filter is adopted. But it cannot work when the single-mode fiber is shortened to 25 m. The results show that the nonlinear fiber laser based on single mode fibers as the Brillouin gain medium is hard to realize ultra-short (<; 10m) caivity, limiting its single-longitudinal-mode operation.

articleTitle: High Power Random Fiber Laser: From Demonstration to Application
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present the demonstration and manipulation of high power random fiber laser (RFL) with unique temporal stability, spectrum and polarization features and the application exploration of RFL in high power MOPA and mid-infrared laser generation.

articleTitle: Compact silicon multicast switch for pCDC ROADM based on thermooptic Mach-Zehnder interferometers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an optimized multicast switch for colorless, directionless and partially contentionless ROADM and experimentally demonstrate a 2×8 silicon multicast switch, which consists of six 3-dB multimode interference splitters and four Mach-Zehnder 2×2 optical switches.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum Generation in Cascaded Photonic Crystal Fiber Tapers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose two-stage cascaded photonic crystal fiber tapers for the supercontinuum (SC) generation. The nonlinear evolution of the SC generation is numerically investigated when pump pulses with different peak powers are used.

articleTitle: 2x2 Polarized MIMO Antenna Selection Based on Correlation Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems with orthogonal electric and magnetic states of polarization is suggested to make full use of antenna dimensions. Generally speaking, lower correlation coefficients between sub-channels result in higher system capacity, yet for polarized MIMO with orthogonal electric and magnetic antenna dipoles, system under ideal condition of zero correlation may perform less than some actual condition with specific correlation coefficients. Specific pairs of antennas of electric or magnetic antenna dipoles are found to be able to achieve such correlation coefficients, which make them perform better than common polarized MIMO antennas.

articleTitle: Fiber Optic Seismic Monitoring System for Highway Rock Slope
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Seismic monitoring is essential for the stability assessment of highway rock slope. This paper presents the design and implementation of a precision fiber optic seismic monitoring system for highway rock slope using fiber Bragg grating geophone and vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser-based interrogator. The overall composition, sensor design and interrogation scheme are introduced in detail. The field test results show that this system has great potential for stability monitoring of highway rock slope.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Fused-Biconical Type Mode Selective Coupler Using Four-Mode Fiber at 1550 nm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this letter, we demonstrate a fused-biconical type mode selective coupler that couples the LP01 mode in single-mode fiber and the high-order modes in four-mode fiber. We also discuss the threshold conditions for HOMs.

articleTitle: A Quantization Scheme by Slicing Supercontinuum Spectrum in an All-Normal Dispersion Silicon Nitride Ridge Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an all normal dispersion silicon nitride waveguide for optical quantization. The results show that a 6-bit quantization resolution is successfully achieved with an effective number of bit of 5.978 bit.

articleTitle: An Image Deblurring Algorithm Based on Edge Selection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In the image deblurring problem, as the blurred images usually have less gradient total contrast than the clear images, the maximum a posterior estimation method prefers to the non-blur interpretation. Hence, this paper focuses on how edge selection can affect blurring kernel estimation, and an image deblurring algorithm based on edge selection is proposed, which can be used to estimate blurring kernel and latent clear image simultaneously under the framework of maximum a posterior probability estimation. Experimental result shows that the proposed algorithm can estimate the optimal blurring kernel, and the restored latent clear image can get better visual experience.

articleTitle: Monitoring The Deflection of Bridge Span With a Spotreduced Fiber Optics Source
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel method to increase the measurement range and accuracy of bridge deflection based on the laser datum scheme with reduced spot size of a fiber source is proposed in this paper. To get rid of the problems of non-circular field distribution and changes of the semiconductor laser caused by heating and temperature, the output of a single mode fiber has been used as the light source of the measurement system. By pulling a normal single mode fiber into a smaller diameter, a stable and small spot light source for monitoring the deflection of bridge span can be obtained in our experiment. The FWHM of the spot at 20 meters distance from the fiber output can be reduced from 1.96mm to 1.62mm when the diameter of the fiber core is tapered from 4.04μm to 1.7μm.By using a spot reduced fiber light source, the range and accuracy of the laser deflection detection system can be effectively improved, thus the proposed scheme has prospect in practical applications.

articleTitle: The fabrication mechanism and spectral characteristics of Fiber Gratings fabricated by point-by-point direct-writing based on femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a series of fiber gratings with different spectrum characteristics are fabricated in standard telecommunication fiber without hydrogen loading by point-by-point direct writing method based on 100 femtosecond laser amplifier system at 800-nm central wavelength. They are including the fourth-order fiber Bragg grating, fiber Bragg grating Fabry-Perot cavity, sampling fiber Bragg grating and cascaded long period fiber grating. The experimental results show that the spectrum characteristics of fourth-order fiber Bragg gratings with Λ=1.93 μm period are obtained at the center wavelength λ=1394.5 nm, and the fiber Bragg grating Fabry-Perot cavity can be inscribed when the gating period is Λ=1.95 μm. Furthermore, the sampled fiber Bragg gratings with different sampled periods are fabricated by adjusting the sampling period. Finally, the spectrum of the cascaded long period fiber gratings is achieved by changing the grating pitch of long period grating with 3 mm, 5 mm and 7 mm, respectively. This study will provide a powerful experimental gist and theoretical basis for the fabrication of different types of fiber gratings by femtosecond laser point-by-point writing directly method.

articleTitle: A Novel Ship-rocking Forecasting Method based on Hilbert Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The ship-rocking is a crucial factor which affects the accuracy of the ocean-based aerospace vehicle measurement. Here we have analysed groups of ship-rocking time series in horizontal and vertical directions utilizing a Hilbert based method from statistical physics. Based on these results we could predict certain amount of future values of the ship-rocking time series based on the current and the previous values. Our predictions are as accurate as the conventional methods from stochastic processes and provide a much wider prediction time range.

articleTitle: Two-color random fiber laser with flexible power proportion based on phosphosilicate fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A two-color random fiber laser based on phosphosilicate fiber with flexible power proportion and 117 nm wavelength interval was demonstrated. The power proportion of the silica-related Stokes light ranged from 99.0 % to 0 %.

Author Keywords: random distributed feedback Raman fiber laser

articleTitle: Development of ultrastable lasers at 1. 5μm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the development of ultrastable lasers at 1.5μm. Through PDH method, the fiber lasers are locked to two ultra-stable optical cavities with finesse of 483000 and 148000 respectively. Through comparing two similar ultrastable laser systems, the linewidth of 0.68Hz and the fractional frequency instability of 2.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> at 1s averaging time are achieved.

articleTitle: The Loss Characteristics of Curved Fiber at Small Radius
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Curved optical fiber sticking onto a round structure has many applications, such as mandrel acoustic sensors and fiber-length scratchable phase modulators. However, the components' performances are limited by the transmission loss of the wound fibers. In this paper, the bending loss characteristic of curved fiber at small radius is theoretically analysed and experimentally demonstrated. A modified five-layer slab waveguide theory is used, which indicates that the bend loss has distinct oscillations at small radius. When the bending radius is smaller, the oscillation period changes more observably. In the experiment, single-mode fiber is bended on the outer surface of cylinders with various radius. The experimental result is consistent with theoretical analysis one.

articleTitle: A novel kind of pulsating soliton in mode-locked fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We find a novel kind of pulsating soliton with broadened Kelly sidebands. By simulation, we find the wavelength of the soliton oscillates due to the interaction with the unsynchronized resonant dispersive wave.

articleTitle: Metal-organic framework based OLED for visible light communication
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Metal organic framework (MOF) materials can encapsulate organic dye molecules and realize new types of OLEDs for VLC system. We present spectrally flat white OLED based on red-yellow-green-blue dye-loaded MOF and linearly polarized warm-yellow MOF-OLED.

articleTitle: High Speed and High Power Photodiode with 50 GHz Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we report a normal incident high speed high power modified uni-traveling carrier photodiode with 3dB bandwidth of 50 GHz and responsivity of 0.1 A/W at -3 V bias voltage.

articleTitle: Fabrication of surface corrugated Long Period Gratings on Plastic Optical Fibers for Refractive Index Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We use a simple way to fabricate surface corrugated long period gratings (LPGs) on commercial plastic optical fibers (POFs) by die press print method. The so-obtained LPGs are proposed as refractive index (RI) sensors in this work. The LPGs imprinted on the POFs with different diameters are evaluated, and it shows that an LPG imprinted on a thin POF (with a diameter of 0.25mm) exhibits better RI sensing performance than that of the ones on thick POFs (with diameters of 0.5 and 1.0mm). When the LPG with period of 100μm, groove depth of 45μm was imprinted on the POF with a diameter of 0.25mm, the RI sensitivity of 1998%/RIU with a resolution of 2.70×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> RIU is obtained. The sensor is a low-cost solution for RI sensing purpose and with the features of simple structure, easy fabrication and intensity modulation at visible wavelengths.

articleTitle: A Burst-mode Optical Amplifier for TWDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: One of the critical challenges for TWDM-PON is that the optical amplifiers need to run in the burst-mode, with an up to 40 dB dynamic range. This presentation discusses the corresponding requirements and solutions.

articleTitle: Electrical degradation behavior in metal oxide thin film transistor under negative bias-illumination stress
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The electrical degradation behavior in metal oxide thin film transistor (TFT) under negative bias-illumination stress (NBIS) is one of the biggest obstacles for its applications in flat panel display. In order to solve this issue, Sr and N are doped in In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> thin film and significantly improve the NBIS stability of In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> TFT. In addition, the doping of N can also reduce the degradation in electrical performance caused by Sr doping. The XPS of SrInON thin film is tested to prove the reduction of the oxygen vacancy.

articleTitle: Output Performance of an Incoherently Pumped Random Fiber Laser Dependence on the Pump Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The output performance of an incoherently pumped random fiber laser (RFL) dependence on the pump bandwidth has been investigated. This work could provide a new pumping scheme for the high power RFLs.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystal Tunable Narrow Linewidth Filter Based On Subwavelength Gratings Reflector
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a electro-tunable liquid crystal (LC) filter consisting of a DBRs and SWGs reflectors which enables uniform alignment of LC. The filter achieve a wide-continuous tuning range of 60 nm and a linewidth of less than 1 nm.

articleTitle: Wavelength Switchable Mode-Locked Fiber Laser with Tapered Two-Mode Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An Er-doped mode-locked fiber laser with a tapered two-mode fiber for wavelength selection has been demonstrated. Depending on the free spectral range of TTMF filter, the central wavelengths of the mode-locking operation can be switched.

articleTitle: Deterministic Single Soliton Generation Driven by Chirped Optical Pulses in Kerr Microresonator
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Deterministic single soliton corresponding to a smooth Kerr combs is more favored in applications. However, precise and rapid control, stochastic solitons number and low conversion efficiency are great challenges in the microresonator (MRR) driven by continuous-wave (c.w.). In this paper, we show that the MRR driving by chirped optical pulse can effectively overcome these issues. Deterministic single soliton can be produced when the chirp parameter is larger than the threshold with proper final pump phase detuning. Once above the threshold, the chirp parameter and pulse duration have no significant effects on the soliton peak power and bandwidth indicating a flexible choice of driving pulse. Nevertheless, the soliton peak power and bandwidth can be simply controlled by the final detuning.

articleTitle: Integrated Biosensor Based on Double-layer Dielectric Loaded Graphene Plasmonic Ridge Waveguide with Higher-Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a double-layer dielectric loaded graphene plasmonic ridge waveguide (DLGPRW) using higher-order modes for biochemical sensing. The simulation results show that the propagation length and the sensing sensitivities are greatly improved.

articleTitle: Strong fiber Bragg grating sensor based on optoelectrical oscillation for ultra-fast and ultra-stable position-finding and measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a quasi-distribute sensor based on optoelectrical oscillator (OEO) incorporating a uniform strong fiber Bragg grating (FBG). When reflection spectrum of FBG moves to longer wavelength due to external changes, the oscillation will occur and the target position will be mapped into the oscillating frequency. Ultrahigh stability of <; 14kHz and ultra-short response time of 1.5s are better than many solutions. The sensing threshold can be tuned linearly with the laser operating wavelength with Pearson's r of 0.9989.

articleTitle: Splicing ET (error-tolerant) Quantum Computing System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we develop a system with redundant splicing topology by studying the ET (error-tolerant) system, and study its unique advantages in topology. And tapped the potential of application in quantum computing. Through theoretical analysis and modeling, it reveals various possibilities for the design of two-dimensional and even three-dimensional quantum computing systems, which are widely neglected in the field of quantum computing, and combines some features of the previous ET system design. And the design methodology is discussed; the network design of the novel quantum computing system can be further introduced into the unique topology.

articleTitle: Multi-path Channel Estimation in Mobile Visible Light Communication Based on Decision Feedback
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In the mobile vehicle network using street lamps, in order to track the time-varying multipath VLC channel, we propose a novel outdoor mobile visible light communication channel estimation method based on decision feedback. With different system parameters, simulations and analysis are carried out. Results show that compared with the conventional scheme, the proposed method can reduce the bit error rate below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, thus effectively improve system performance for the mobile VLC channel.

articleTitle: Real-time observation of Q-switched mode-locking dynamics in a fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The build-up of a self-started stretched-pulse fiber laser was experimentally investigated using time-stretched dispersive Fourier transform spectroscopy. Interestingly, soliton pulsations were observed in a rich set of clustered Q-switching bunches in the turbulent and rapidly-evolving pre-mode-locking states of the laser.

articleTitle: High-Dynamic Optical Network Control Architecture Based on Spatiotemporal Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a novel high-dynamic optical network control architecture based on spatiotemporal synchronization. By introducing high-precision time synchronization, control coordination among nodes and controllers can be established to improve the network dynamic performance by orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Research on the degradation of perovskite thin films based on spectrometric ellipsometry
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The power conversion efficiency of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has jumped over 23%. However, the stability of perovskites is still a major obstacle for its commercialization. In order to explore the optical degradation process of perovskite materials, the spectrometric ellipsometry (SE) was used to study the optical properties change of perovskite film caused by degradation. Humidity is the main degradation factor to be considered. First, the CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> perovskite thin films were prepared on sapphire substrate by one-step spin coating method. Second, SE was used to obtain the spectral response curves with wavelength-range from 210 nm to 1690 nm. Perovskite films were measured a few times at 65° incident angle under ambient condition (Temperature:21°C; Relative Humidity:80%)by SE. Then, the optical models of the films were modelled by Tauc-Lorentz model and the measured curves were fitted to obtain the changes of optical constants with degradation. As a result, when the wavelength is less than 700nm, the spectral curves of CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> gradually descend but ascend with the wavelength when the wavelength is more than 700nm after 30 days. The experimental results show that spectrometric ellipsometry can reflect the changes in optical characteristics during the degradation of perovskite thin films. Analysing the change of the optical properties can help reveal the degradation mechanism of perovskite materials.

articleTitle: Improving Multicast Routing Performance in Surface Wave Optical Network-on-Chip
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Considering the broadcasting communication feature of surface wave, we construct a two-layer hybrid ONoC architecture, and a multicast routing strategy suitable for this architecture is also proposed.

articleTitle: A novel hypergraph structured optical network model
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: After entering the 21st century, the annual growth rate of network bandwidth demand is as high as 50-100%. In recent years, Automatic Switch Optical Network (ASON) have been widely studied as a new generation optical network technology with high speed, large capacity and ultra-long distance transmission. Among them, the main research focuses on improving the network bandwidth and transmission rate. However, due to the increasingly stable transmission medium and mode, the improvement of research results is very limited, especially in the current situation of a large number of network nodes. In order to improve the performance of optical network, a new structure model of optical network hypergraph is proposed based on Wavelength Division Multiplex (WDM) and Hypergraph theory. In addition, the routing based on parallel-path-based bandwidth algorithm (PPBA) demonstrates the excellent topology characteristics of the network, such as small diameter, low blocking rate and short forwarding delay.

articleTitle: A tunable dual-frequency optoelectronic oscillator based on opical FBG-FP filter and electrical YIG filter
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel scheme of dual-frequency optoelectronic oscillator based on fiber Bragg grating Fabry-Perot (FBG-FP) filter and YIG filter is proposed and proved by experiment. Each frequency can be tuned independently in a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Triple Closed-Loop Resonant Fiber Optic Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To improve the reciprocity of the signal processing systems, a triple closed-loop resonant fiber optic gyroscope is proposed. Enhanced long-term and thermal bias stabilities are successfully demonstrated thanks to the reciprocal configuration.

articleTitle: Economical Solution for Cladding Etched Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an economical wet etching solution for optical fibers using glass etching cream. The etching performance and surface quality on optical fibers are investigated. The solution offers good controllability and repeatable outcomes.

articleTitle: Research on Strong Background Light Suppression Technology Based on Power Inversion
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Because the direct background light generated by the sun is strong, its strong background light power is much higher than the LED's power, and the signal is completely submerged in the background noise, causing communication interruption. To solve the above problems, this paper establishes a visible light communication system between LED traffic lights and vehicles under strong background light, and introduces the power inversion algorithm into the system to suppress the influence of strong background light, then analyzes and compares the bit error rate of the systems under different signal-to-interference ratio. The simulation results show that the power inversion using the 3-element receiving array can generate a null of about -70dB in the direction of strong background light, so that the noise value of the output is significantly reduced, the signal gain remains unchanged. When the signal interference ratio of system is -15, the BER is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, which can supply the need of communication.

articleTitle: Enhanced Magneto-Optical Effects in Magnetic Photonic Crystal Fiber Based on Yttrium Iron Garnet
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a kind of magnetic photonic crystal fiber of Yttrium iron garnet (YIG) is presented. The influence of gyrotropy on TE-TM mode conversion is analysed, which depends on Faraday rotation. The structure parameters are simulated and optimized. The optimum efficiency of 93.57% is obtained. Faraday rotation and modal birefringence have been calculated by varying gyrotropy from 0.01 to 0.04. The numerical results reveal an increased Faraday rotation and a reduced modal birefringence of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>. The enhanced properties of the structure could improve photonic devices performance, which make it suitable for magneto-optical isolators.

articleTitle: Optimized Quantum Dot Light-emitting-device with Insulating Layer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We reported the preparation of CdSe/CdS/ZnS based quantum dot light-emitting-devices (QLED) with an ultra-thin PMMA layer. This PMMA layer between the quantum dots layer and the electron-transport layer retards the electron current and results in a more balanced electron and hole injecting into emissive quantum dot layer. The optimized charge balance enhanced the device external quantum efficiency (EQE). The results show that the precise control of the PMMA layer thickness is quite important, otherwise, leading to degraded device efficiency and increased turn on voltage.

articleTitle: Study on Temperature Rise Characteristic of LED Lighting Fixture under Different Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The temperature rise characteristic of LED lighting fixture under different conditions was studied in the paper. The experimental results showed that the temperature rise of LED lighting fixture under the condition of with cover and no dust was about 1.5 times higher than that of LED lighting fixture under the condition of no cover and with dust. Apparently, the influence of the cover on the heat dissipation of LED lighting fixture was much larger than the dust.

articleTitle: Capacity Expansion based Network Failure Recovery with Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To overcome the network bottleneck when a failure occurs, a capacity expansion based recovery model is established, and is solved by genetic algorithm under link recovery and path recovery strategies, achieving the minimal network expansion cost.

articleTitle: Bend performance of single trench large mode area fiber with step-index core
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Bend performance of a single trench large mode area fiber with a step-index core is investigated. The step-index core is introduced to modulate the distribution of the fundamental mode. Numerical results demonstrate the designed fiber can achieve a high loss ratio (as high as 886) at the wavelength of 2 μm when the bend radius is only 10 cm.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive RI and temperature sensor based on cascaded LPGs at near the phase-matching turning point
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a highly sensitivity refractive index (RI) and temperature sensor based on cascaded long-period gratings (LPGs) operating at near the phase-matching turning point (PMTP). A series of narrow resonance peaks formed by interference between cladding mode and core mode showed relative high Q-factor comparison with the one of the LPG. The experimental results showed that such fiber sensor have RI sensitivity of 1360nm/RIU@1.33 and 3669.7nm/RIU@1.41 and the temperature sensitivity of 4.079 nm/°C.

articleTitle: Efficient and Range-Variable Laser Wireless Charging Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The conversion efficiency of photovoltaic cells, charging distance and tracking technology are three important indicators of laser wireless charging technology. This paper demonstrates an efficient laser wireless charging scheme with variable charging distance and a simple tracking system. The laser wireless charging system proposed in this paper is mainly composed of 808nm laser, zoom beam expander, GaAs photovoltaic cell and energy management module. By increasing the uniformity of laser spot energy distribution, the conversion efficiency of GaAs photovoltaic cells reaches 35.3%. Reduce system cost by simplifying the tracking system. Using zoom beam expander, the charging distance ranges from 10 to 50 meters.

articleTitle: Speckle-free high contrast bio-imaging in dental hard tissue using random fiber laser in backscattering configuration
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The size or depth of the dental caries could be underestimated by conventional dental caries detection method, such as radiography. In this paper, backscattering tooth imaging method based on near infrared random fiber laser has been investigated. We demonstrate that the random fiber laser is ideally suitable for dental caries diagnosis owing to its near infrared wavelength, high spectral density and low coherence.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Fiber Optic Pressure Sensor Based on Silica Diaphragm Fabricated by MEMS
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents the fabrication procedure of a 1.2-μm thick silica diaphragm with high uniformity using microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technique. The diaphragm fabrication started from a commercially available double-polished 300-μm silicon wafer with a silica layer on its bottom. The silica diaphragm was released from the wafer by photolithography, wet etching and inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching. A fiber optic Fabry-Perot (FP) pressure sensor was made by thermally bonding the diaphragm to the end face of an etched fiber with an outside diameter of 125 μm. The obtained sensor has a static pressure sensitivity of 12.4 nm/kPa (85.3 nm/psi). It has a great potential to work in medical applications where miniature size and high sensitivity are essential.

articleTitle: Adaptive Bandwidth Allocation Strategy for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Traditional bandwidth allocation methods mainly allocate bandwidth according to the priority information of different service data, however, such strategy cannot grantee detailed granularity, making the bandwidth division unable to be allocated in unit time. This paper proposes an adaptive network bandwidth allocation strategy for satellite communication, which transforms the priority of service data to the maximum transmission time for different scale data. And then, a greedy strategy according to the weight has been introduced for encapsulating channels, which can be mapped to the randomized time-varying knapsack problem. Experiments on synthetic data prove that the strategy can effectively allocate the limited bandwidth, and improve the data transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Temperature sensitive Properties of Eu2+/ Mn2+ Co-doped Ca2Sr (PO4)2
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>/Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> co-doped Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr(PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> phosphors were synthesized by high temperature solid-state method. It was studied by X-ray diffraction, room temperature and high temperature photoluminescence spectra. The results show that an effective energy transfer is existed in this phosphors from Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> to Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>. Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> / Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> co-doped Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr (PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) 2 phosphors have excellent optical temperature sensing properties. Two well-separated emission peaks which can be used as signal identification are exieted in emission spectrum. Absolute sensitivity and relative sensitivity are in direct proportion to temperature. Both absolute sensitivity and relative sensitivity can be improved at the same time. Therefore, Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr (PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>: Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 +</sup>, Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 +</sup> has potential application prospect.

articleTitle: A sensitivity enhanced Sagnac temperature sensor utilizing high order modes interference
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A temperature sensor is proposed by splicing a section of thin polarization-maintaining fiber in a Sagnac loop. The temperature sensitivity is enhanced by higher- order modes interference and reaches up to 1.7 nm/□.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of atmospheric channel reciprocity in fiber receiving systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper designs a reciprocity measurement system for atmospheric channel for the first time in China. The mean of reciprocity is higher than 0.8, which proves that the atmospheric channel has strong reciprocity. The research in this paper provides a parameter reference for adaptive optics system design.

articleTitle: Performance of Bi-Directional Mode-Locked Fiber Laser at 2 μm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Bidirectional mode-locking pulse laser has attracted great attentions because of its simplicity and compactness for free-running dual-comb spectroscopy. In this paper, we developed an all-polarization- maintaining, bi-directional Tm-doped fiber laser at 2 μm with a single-wall carbon nanotube (SWNT) presented as saturable absorber mode-locking mechanism. By manipulating the polarization controller, changing the pump power and shortening the cavity length, we successfully obtain bidirectional mode-locking operations at different repetition frequencies, namely 35 MHz and 122 MHz. Besides, the repetition rate difference between the clockwise and counterclockwise pulse trains is adaptable, varying from 764 Hz to 1.01 KHz at 35 MHz and 540 Hz to 1.8 KHz at 122 MHz.

articleTitle: Physical Encryption Based on Chaotic Sequence-assisted Pseudo QAM Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a physical encryption scheme based on chaotic sequence-assisted pseudo quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) systems. We simulated the proposed scheme and verified its feasibility by plotting BER curves and constellation diagrams.

articleTitle: Mach-Zehnder interferometer in no-core fiber based on femtosecond laser inscribed waveguides
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer constructed by femtosecond laser written waveguides in no-core fiber. Such an interferometer device consists of a section of no-core fiber, fusion spliced with single mode fiber at its two ends. One of the interferometer arms is formed by the waveguide inscribed and the other follows the diverging light path inside the no-core fiber before arriving at the end of single mode fiber core. Such a device based on internal structure can be used not only for temperature and strain, but also for external refractive index measurement.

articleTitle: Exciplex emission based on Lewis acid-base interaction
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We exemplify a new exciplex emission system based on an appropriate electron donor (35DCzPPy) and a Lewis acid borane B(C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> as electron acceptor. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy proved that N-B bond formed between 35DCzPPy and B(C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, which make the charge transfer process more efficient. By the Lewis acid-base interaction, B(C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> has achieved blue-light emitting by the excited state intermolecular charge transfer process.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of a wide detection range refractive index sensor based on exposed core tellurite micro-structured optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel refractive index (RI) sensor based on the multimode interference effect in an exposed-core tellurite microstructure optical fiber (TMOF) has been designed and implemented in this paper. With different liquid analytes covered onto TMOF core surface, the interference between any two specific modes experiences a fringe shift (or phase change). The exposed-core optical fiber design provides direct access to the evanescent field, allowing RI measurement with a sensitivity of up to 2919.4 nm/RIU. The proposed sensor offers a higher sensitivity while maintaining the fiber robustness and a much wider RI detection range (reaching to 1.58) than its existing counterparts based on multimode interference effect of traditional silica optical fiber. It is also reliable, cost-effective and offers a possibility for label-free biosensing.

articleTitle: Temperature-insensitive Fiber Twist Sensor Based on A Reflective Microfiber Coupler
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A temperature-insensitive fiber twist sensor based on a reflective microfiber coupler with a high sensitivity of 2621.08 (a.u.)/(rad/m) is demonstrated. Modal interference of the sensor is analysed by Fast Fourier transform algorithm.

articleTitle: Generation of L-band Vector Soliton from Dispersion-managed Er-doped Mode-locked Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The polarization-locked L-band vector solitons were generated from dispersion-managed Er-doped fiber laser incorporating with carbon nanotubes for the first time. The vector solitons operate at wavelength near 1594.7 nm with repetition rate of 12.13 MHz.

articleTitle: A Fiber Bragg Grating-based Wind Erosion Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a wind erosion monitoring system includes a shunt-hedging and cyclone-separation sand sampler built by Fluent and a weighting sensor based on FBG. According to the simulation and experiment, this system had anti strong wind interference performance and it could measure in real time, passively, continuously, and in a long distance.

articleTitle: Design of Metamaterial Microstrip Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a new type of metamaterial structure based on open resonant ring is proposed. On this basis, a microstrip array antenna based on metamaterial is designed and simulated by HFSS.

articleTitle: Optically Adjustable Random Laser With Multi-phase Shifted Bragg Grating in Er/Yb Co-doped Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optically controllable Er/Yb co-doped random fiber laser with a random multi-phase shifted fiber Bragg grating pumped by a 980 nm laser is proposed. We used a 980 nm laser diode to laterally pump an Er/Yb co-doped fiber with a random multi-phase shifted fiber Bragg grating. Through changing lateral pump location, control of laser outputs was achieved. As a result, outputs of one or two main laser peaks were obtained by changing the locations of the Er/Yb co-doped fiber being laterally pumped.

articleTitle: Circuit System Design of Handheld Near Infrared Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a short overview on the building principles of novel handheld systems will be provided.According to the spectrometer test results, the circuit system can meet the line array CMOS drive of near-infrared spectrometer, spectral data acquisition and transmission. The circuit system has been designed to realize linear array CMOS driving of near-infrared spectrometer, acquisition and transmission of spectral data. In addition, SNR of the circuit system is as high as 555.35 which can be Suitable for near infrared spectrometer applications.

articleTitle: Wavelength selective saturation in optical absorption of array of self-organized InAs/GaAs QDs
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a photocurrent study of a p-i-n GaAs diode incorporating InAs self-organized quantum dots (QDs) in the intrinsic region. In two-color experiments the possibility of spectral hole burning in the QD absorption spectrum by means of resonant excitation of the dot states is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Auto-correction Method for Incident Light Instability and Temperature 3D Display Technology in RDTS
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel temperature demodulation method which eliminates the unstable of incident light on Raman distributed temperature sensors (RDTS) is presented. This method based on the incident light fluctuation compensation algorithm which optimizes the temperature measurement errors for RDTS. Besides, compared to convention temperature-distance display method, the temperature three-dimensional (3D) display technology can realize the fibre model 3D display. Experimental results indicate that the temperature measurement error is optimized by using the presented method. This paper provides a solution for accurate measurement of temperature as well as temperature 3D display along the sensing fibre for RDTS systems.

articleTitle: Large-scale arrayed waveguide grating router for T-band communication
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The T-band (1000-1260 nm), which offers more than 60 THz worth of bandwidth and wider than C- and L-band combined. The large scale photonic router using 3-stage arrayed-waveguide grating for T-band and O-band is configured.

articleTitle: Mode-locked Pulsed Fiber Laser with Graphene Solution as Saturable Absorber Deposited in Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate mode-locked Erbium doped fiber laser (EDFL) by incorporating graphene filled photonic crystal fiber (PCF) into the laser cavity. The 1.5 cm long PCF filled with graphene solution acts as a saturable absorber (SA) to produce pulse with repetition rate of 11.1 MHz and pulse width of 0.88 ps.

articleTitle: A Novel Chaos-Based Three-Dimensional Constellation Rotation Encryption Algorithm for OFDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: fibre optic sensors; fibre lasers; optical modulation; Bragg gratings; laser cavity resonators; laser mode locking; diffraction gratings; optical fibre networks; optical pumping; error statistics.

articleTitle: Optimized Sensitivity Analysis of Phase Modulated Optical Fiber Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Influence of different oxide overlayers on the performance of phase modulated optical fiber sensor coated with graphene is reported. The simulation model is constructed according to the the transmission matrix theory. In this work, we improve the phase sensitivity of the sensor by adding different oxides coatings include magnesium oxide (MgO), aluminum oxide (Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>), lutetium oxide (Lu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>), scandium oxide (Sc<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) and tellurium dioxide (TeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) on the surface of monolayer graphene. The phase sensitivity of the sensor is optimized by the type and thickness of oxide coating. The phase sensitivity of the sensor with 35 nm TeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> coating on the surface of monolayer graphene achieved 1.3467 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>deg/RIU.

articleTitle: Security authentication based on generated address algorithm for software-defined optical communication network
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the rapid increase in the number of optical line terminals (OLTs) and optical network units (ONUs) connected to the control center in the software defined optical access network (SDOAN) environment, the security problems caused by the communication between devices and the high cost caused by the introduction of security schemes, we propose a lightweight identity two-way authentication scheme (LTWA) based on the cryptographically generated address (CGA) algorithm combined with the hash generated address (HGA) algorithm. The scheme introduces the CGA algorithm and the HGA algorithm without third party participation, so as to complete the first authentication binding and the non-first authentication binding between the communication nodes respectively, which effectively prevents an attacker from forging or tampering with authentication interaction messages, thereby establishing an end-to-end trusted connection in the access network.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Service Function Chainings Mapping Algorithm Based on Betweenness Centralities
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To effectively solve the problem about how to map service function chainings (SFCs) in data center over elastic optical network (DC-EON), a comprehensive service function chainings mapping algorithm based on betweenness centralities (CSM-BC) is proposed, which aims at assisting the mapping of both virtual nodes and links in network function virtualization (NFV) scenarios, corresponding to virtual network function (VNF) deployments and virtual link routing with spectrum allocations, respectively. This proposed algorithm concurrently considers betweenness centralities of DC nodes, reuses of VNFs and comprehensive link weights in the substrate network to accomplish SFCs mapping. The simulation results indicate that CSM-BC deploys fewer VNFs and occupies less spectral units than existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Study of temperature controlling of a solid Fabry–Pérot etalon
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The solid Fabry-Pérot etalon is a widely used optical passive device in optical communications. However, the optical characteristics of Fabry-Pérot etalons are temperature dependent. In this study, we designed a temperature Insulation structure and employed a PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controlling algorithm. The temperature influence on the etalon transmission spectrum is also discussed according to its temperature characteristics. By analyzing the experimental data, the effects of temperature control and non-temperature control on the Fabry-Pérot etalon were compared.

articleTitle: High-power linearly-polarized supercontinuum generation from few-mode polarization-maintaining photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a high-power broadband linearly-polarized supercontinuum (LP-SC) laser source by coupling the output of a polarization-maintaining picosecond master oscillator power amplifier (PM-MOPA) at 1064 nm into a few-mode polarization-maintaining photonic crystal fiber (PM-PCF). The PM-MOPA delivers 150 ps pulses at a high repetition rate of 80 MHz with 120.4 W average output power. The short wavelength band of LP-SC is extended from 580 nm to 480 nm with the aid of intermodal four wave mixing (FWM). The spectrum is finally broadened to 480 -2400 nm with a maximum average power of 77.4 W. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of such a high average power LP-SC generated from PM-PCF with a wide spectrum.

articleTitle: Polarization-insensitive Waveguide Crossings Based on SWGs-assisted MMI
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A polarization-insensitive waveguide crossing based on sub-wavelength gratings (SWGs) assisted multimode interference (MMI) is proposed and demonstrated on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform. The proposed device is characterized with low insertion loss and low crosstalk for both TE and TM polarizations from 1500 nm to 1600 nm, 0.69 dB (0.61 dB) for TE (TM) at 1550 nm. The device can be fabricated with single etch process to achieve a footprint of 12.5×12.5 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Further analysis shows that the device has a fabrication tolerance of ±30 nm for the MMI structure. The proposed device can be employed in photonic integrated circuits with polarization-division-(de)multiplexing functionality.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensing based on claddingless fiber and core-offset structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A Mach-Zehnder interferometer based on singlemode- claddingless - singlemode core-offset structure is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The experimental results show that the refractive index sensitivity is 162.64 nm/refractive index unit (RIU). The proposed sensor is high mechanical strength, low cost and easy manufacturing, which will make a significant contribution to RI measurement. And it has the good potential applications in physical, chemical and other sensing fields.

articleTitle: The effect of position of ytterbium-doped fiber on the output spectrum of random fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The effect of ytterbium-doped fiber on the output spectrum of a random fiber laser is analyzed and discussed in this paper. The experimental results show that putting ytterbium-doped fiber in the random fiber laser's cavity is beneficial for the generation of high-order Stokes. A near-infrared supercontinuum with 20dB bandwidth of more than 500nm can be generated, which proved that a random laser fiber not only can works as a traditional random fiber laser, but also can be a novel, simple, low cost, low coherence, and robust near-infrared supercontinuum generation method.

articleTitle: Photon correlation method for acoustic pressure measurement in free sound field
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Microphones are calibrated by reciprocity method currently, but not for the nonstandard size microphones. To solve the calibration problem for nonstandard microphones, research on a non-invasive optical method for acoustic pressure measurement in free sound field. By auto-correlating scattered photon sequences, the particle velocity can be measured, and further acquiring the acoustic pressure at certain position. Experiment results show , the difference between photon correlation method and standard microphone is within 0.61 dB when the acoustic frenquency is between 200Hz and 8kHz, verifying the feasibility of the correlation method.

articleTitle: The Power-dependent Phase Change in a Low-bias High-speed Modified Uni-traveling Carrier Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The characterization of the phase change of 60-GHz sinusoidal in the modified uni-traveling carrier photodetector is reported. The absolute phase change is observed smallest when the differential capacitance equals to zero.

articleTitle: Measurement of the position and orientation of mechanical arm based on laser tracker
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The estimation of position and orientation measurement method of mechanical arm based on laser tracker is implemented. The dynamic measurement method is introduced to estimate the position and orientation of dynamic targets, acquired by laser tracker, in the space. Moreover, the angle and trajectory information can be real-time derived with software so that the differences between the designed and the measured angle can be obtained. The experimental results show the consistency with the designed parameters. The fluctuation of rotational angle caused by movement is less than 1° and meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: A fiber etched cavity for microsphere whispering-gallery-mode excitation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a whispering-gallery-mode microsphere resonator. The device is fabricated by fusion splicing of a section of no-core fiber with multi-mode fiber and single-mode fiber at its two ends. The open end of multimode fiber is etched to create an arc shaped cavity, with a microsphere glued at its bottom. The device has a Q-factor of 1.21 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, is robust in structure and of low cost.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Resonant Frequency of an Optical Fiber Vector Sensor with Different Packages
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The characteristic of resonant frequency of three different optical fiber vector sensors (OFVS) operating in water were studied. The effect of package types (spherical and cylindrical) and package masses are considered. The experimental results show that there are two resonant peaks in the OFVS, which were not reported in previous studies. A new model shall be proposed to characterize the performance of OFVS operating in some medium.

articleTitle: Narrow-Linewidth Photonic Microwave Generation Based on an Optically Injected Semiconductor Laser Subject to Subharmonic Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a scheme to acquire a narrow-linewidth photonic microwave based on an optically injected semiconductor laser (OISL) modulated by a subharmonic microwave from an optoelectronic oscillation (OEO). The microwave frequency generated by the OEO is 7.62 GHz, and the period-one (P1) oscillation frequency of the OISL is close to twice of it. Through modulating the OISL by a 1/2 subharmonic microwave generated by the OEO, the photonic microwave is locked at 15.24 GHz with a 3-dB linewidth about 1 kHz and a SSB phase noise of -94 dBc/Hz at offset frequency 10 kHz.

articleTitle: Direct oscillation of ultrafast HOM in Yb-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated direct oscillation of high order modes (HOMs) in a mode-locking Yb-doped fiber laser, in which a pair of mode-selective couplers act as an efficient mode conversion centered around 1064 nm.

articleTitle: On-demand design of nanophotonic gratings using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The design of nanophotonic structures relies on solving the Maxwell’s equation and sweeping parameters in order to obtain the desired properties. The inverse problem, the retrieval of the appropriate parameters from the required electromagnetic responses, remains challenging and time consuming. Here we report on-demand design of photonic gratings using a recurrent neural network. By using back propagation neural network model, we show that a nanophotonic grating can be designed and optimized with predesignated responses. We expect this work will advance the applications of deep learning algorithms in the design of nanophotonic devices.

articleTitle: A FSO Transmission System Based on Partially Coherent Beam Source
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally demonstrated a 4Gbit/s transmission experiment using a low noise partially coherent beam (PCB) source based on wide-spectrum filtered from supercontinuum (SC) which generated from picosecond mode-locked fiber laser pumping highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF). The noise of PCB source is reduced by filtering out amplified spontaneous emission noise of erbium-doped fiber amplifier The eye pattern and eye SNR based on PCB source before and after turbulent channel are measured, respectively. The experimental results show that the SNR of the PCB source before and after turbulent channel are 21.54dB and 17.89dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Radiation Calibration Uncertainty of Multi-Band Polarization Imager
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The principle of multi-band polarization imager is introduced. In order to verify the accuracy, instrument was tested and analyzed by radiation calibration. The radiation calibration accuracy is better than 2%, which meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: Simultaneous measurement of temperature and pressure based on Fabry Perot and Antiresonant mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber-optic sensor for simultaneous measurement of temperature and pressure is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The sensor is composed of a hollow core fiber (HCF) sandwiched by two segments of single mode fiber (SMF), in which Fabry-Perot interference (FPI) combined with antiresonant (AR) mechanism are applied to the simultaneous measurement of temperature and pressure. The reflection spectrum of the sensor is composed of a sinusoid caused by axial FPI and several resonant wavelengths induced by AR mechanism occurred in cladding of the HCF. Two kinds of mechanisms have different responses to temperature and pressure, so the proposed sensor can simultaneously measure the pressure and temperature without pressure-temperature cross-talk. The advantages of the proposed sensor including small size, compact structure, and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: All few-mode fiber passively mode-locked figure-8 cavity laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an all few-mode fiber passively mode-locked figure-8 cavity laser. The hand-made mode division multiplexing-mode selective coupler makes it possible for LP11 mode at 976 nm to be used as pump light source.

articleTitle: Time-Division based Scheduling Scheme for Hybrid Optical/Electrical Data Center Network
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Past few years have witnessed the great development of Optical Circuit Switches (OCSes), which support high and dynamic bandwidth at low per-bit overhead in the data center network. Although OCSes deliver variety of attractive properties, the challenge still remains due to the unneglectable reconfiguration delay of OCSes. Previous OCS-based proposals amortize the long reconfiguration overhead by reconfiguring OCSes at intervals of a few 100s of milliseconds, which inevitably incurs a mass of packets waiting during reconfiguration intervals, hence the degradation of network performance happens. In this paper, we propose an OCS-based scheduling scheme named Time-Division Scheduling (TDS), which groups OCSes and reconfigures different groups in sequential time slots, instead of periodically reconfiguring all OCSes. TDS diminishes the impact of the long reconfiguration delay with mere directly software modifications. We evaluate the performance of TDS via OMNET++. The experimental results show that TDS delivers significant performance enhancements in latency and benefits slightly on the throughput.

articleTitle: Effectiveness Evaluation Model of Laser/Microwave Satellite Communication System Based on Ambient Fuzzy Operator
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Effectiveness evaluation model based on ambient fuzzy operator is proposed for laser/microwave satellite communication system (L/MSCS), in order to evaluate the effectiveness of L/MSCS more scientifically. In this paper, the model establishes an ambient parameter system, and selects the ambient state according to the actual situation of L/MSCS, and then selects the ambient fuzzy operator according to the state. The effectiveness of L/MSCS is simulated by this model and compared with the basic fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (fuzzy-AHP). The research results show that the proposed model is closer to the actual situation and more scientific than fuzzy-AHP.

articleTitle: Study on Connotation of Generalized Aperture Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper establishes a unified description of radar imaging based on spatial spectrum theory. Firstly, the concept of generalized aperture imaging is presented. Then, the combined effect of aperture and signal bandwidth affecting spatial resolution of target is discussed. Moreover, the contribution of the transceiver configuration and signal bandwidth to the inversion result can be defined according to the spatial spectrum filling form of observed echoes. Finally, the connotation of generalized aperture imaging is applied for three typical radar systems, and the corresponding imaging performances are analyzed, which have the advantages of simplicity, clarity and intuitive physical meaning, etc.

articleTitle: Dynamics of asymmetric soliton explosions in ultrafast fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Asymmetric soliton explosions are numerically demonstrated in an all-normal-dispersion Yb-doped mode-locked fiber laser based on a lumped model. It is found that the explosion events manifest themselves when the pump strength is tuned to reside between stationary dissipative soliton and noise-like pulse regimes. Remarkably, although the initial conditions and the model itself are symmetric, the explosions occur only at one edge of the soliton, i.e., the pulse leading and trailing edges explode alternately. Our results pave the way for further investigation on the dynamics of soliton explosions in ultrafast fiber lasers.

articleTitle: Functional-Link Neural Network Based Nonlinear Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
