abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a simple and versatile nonlinear equalizer based on functional-link neural network in a 128-Gb/s single carrier dual-polarization 16-QAM signal transmission over 600 km. The BER can be reduced by half.

articleTitle: High-power vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser with a metal/DBR hybrid reflector
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The design and fabrication of a hybrid metal– semiconductor Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) for optically pumped vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser(VCSEL) are proposed. This structure can decrease the series resistance, and improve the output power of VCSEL.

articleTitle: Single Bandpass Microwave Photonic Filter based on Gain-switched Distributed-feedback Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a single bandpass microwave photonic filter (MPF) based on a gain-switched distributed feedback (DFB) laser is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Self-phase modulation (SPM) effect is explored in the optical domain to enhance the performance of the proposed MPF. A single passband is achieved for the proposed MPF, which can be tuned from 1 GHz to 39 GHz. A theoretical model describing the principle of the proposed MPF is derived, which is confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: High sensitivity biosensor for Staphylococcus Aureus detection based on tapered a singlemode-no core-singlemode fiber structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber biosensor based on tapered singlemode-no core-singlemode (SNS) fiber structure was investigated for the detection of staphylococcus aureus. The fibre sensor was functionalised by depositing the pig IgG antibodies onto tapered biosensor surface, which has specific binding with staphylococcus aureus. The experimental results showed that transmission spectrum of functionalized sensor undergone wavelength blue shift when it was immersed into Staphylococcus aureus solution, and 1.1 nm wavelength shift was observed with a concentration of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>colony-forming units (CFU)/mL.

articleTitle: Joint optimization of amplitude shifting and clipping for KK receiver
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To minimize the devastating zero-by noise effect of KK receiver, amplitude shifting and clipping are coordinated with optimal configuration. And it improves 3-dB sensitivity at 6-dB CSPR for 112-Gbps QAM16 signal after 80-km SSMF.

articleTitle: Resonance Energy Leakage in Hollow Core Fiber for Sensitive Liquid Level Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A sensitive liquid-level sensor based on energy leakage of anti-resonant reflecting guidance in a hollow core fiber is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. It is constructed by splicing a 15mm-long hollow core fiber with a cladding thickness of 40 μm to single mode fibers. Since the leakage of resonance energy is sensitive to surrounding liquids, liquid level is measured by pushing sensor transversely against the liquid surface to efficiently change the proportion of fiber circumference in liquid. Based on the variation of transmission power at resonant wavelengths, liquid-level measurement was achieved with sensitivity up to 7.64 dB/mm, which is several times higher than that of normal sensors immersed vertically into the liquid.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Scheme for Geometrically-shaped Constellation Classification utilizing Support Vector Machine in Multi-access Internet of Vehicle Lighting
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-access Internet of Vehicles (IoV) scheme based on multi-band DFTS-OFDM VLC system. The experimental results show that with the bandwidth of 62.5MHz, the dynamic range was enhanced 1.6 dBm employing SVM in hexagonal constellation Geometrically-shaped (GS) 16QAM and the overall capacity is 250Mbps.

articleTitle: PEG based Construction of Irregular QC-LDPC Codes by jointly Optimizing the Girth and the Number and ACE of Short cycles
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the construction of irregular QC-LDPC codes by jointly optimizing the girth, the number and approximate cycle extrinsic message degree (ACE) of short cycles to further improve the error-floor performance of irregular QC-LDPC codes with given degree distributions. By selecting the best edges, each of which must make the cycles consisting of the current variable node have the best lower bound of ACE or the minimum number of cycles with ACE lower bound, for each variable node via the progressive Edge growth (PEG) approaches, irregular QC-LDPC codes with better tradeoff between girth, the shortest cycle number and ACE could be constructed. Simulation results show that the proposed codes achieve better error-floor performance compared with the codes using the same degree distributions constructed by the recent proposed methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on the Influence of Quantum Dot Display and Liquid Crystal Display on Human Visual Function
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Previous studies have shown that liquid crystal display (LCD) can cause visual fatigue to the human eye, but the effect of quantum dot (QD) display has not been explored yet. This study conducted a human factor experiment on the QD display and LCD. The parameters ACC, HOAs and MTF were selected as objective physiological indicators for visual quantification of visual fatigue. 39 participants performed a 45-minute video viewing task. While before and after the visual task, measured the physiological parameters of the participants' eyes. Analysis the effects of QD display and LCD on human physiological characteristics under the same conditions. The results show that: (1) The QD display and LCD have an influence on the physiological characteristics of the human eye during continuous visual task duration. These effects can be quantified by changes in human eye physiological parameters; (2) The effect of QD display on human eye physiological parameters is less than LCD: the VICO index (visual comfort index) is lower, and the participants' color feedback accuracy is higher. This study provides theoretical basis and data support for the subsequent development of quantum dot display.

articleTitle: Accurate, Fast and Robust Beam Characterization for Fiber Beams Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fiber beam characterization based on deep learning, including mode decomposition and M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> evaluation, has been first-ever demonstrated by simulation and experiment. Deep learning enables not only high accuracy and speed but also high anti-noise ability.

articleTitle: Research on Laser Cavity Ring-down Spectroscopy and Fiber-Based Measurement for SF6 Decomposed Gases
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The four species gases including H2S, CO, HF and SO2 in the decomposition gas of SF6 were monitored online, according to the power industry requirements. The calibration technology and the algorithm, the optical path of cavity and signal to noise ratio of detection circuit are the key steps in the development of decomposed gas monitoring device. This paper first introduces the calibration method and technology of multi-component trace gas analysis instrument based on photo-acoustic spectroscopy. An on-line monitoring device for SF6 decomposition gas based on the laser absorption spectroscopy is developed. The calibration algorithm is proposed and verified by experiment. Within the range of 0~200ppm, the stability is less than 2%. The concentration calibration method proposed in this paper can effectively monitor the concentration of H2S, CO, HF, SO2 typical characteristic gases, and provide theoretical and technical guidance for SF6 gas insulated high-voltage combined electrical apparatus.

articleTitle: An analysis of the abnormal condition of photoelectric deviation of a task on ship-borne equipments
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, Aim at measuring ship at some the accuracy authenticate process front the one mission measure equipments USB Photoelectric deviation abnormality of problem, analysis equipments light axis and electricity axis calibration condition, comb many times mission Photoelectric deviation variety of circumstance, pass ratio to analysis, gradually row check a problem, end fixed position USB equipments Photoelectric deviation value abnormality of reason, find out understanding measure definitely, for follow-up mission data processing error margin revise provide basis.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase difference of acceleration fiber optic vector hydrophone based on signal-to-noise ratio
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and frequency on the phase difference of the acceleration fiber optic vector hydrophone is analyzed and verified by simulation, laboratory measurement and experimental data at sea.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Chaotic Ultra-Wideband Fiber Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A long-distance high-rate chaotic ultra-wideband fiber communication system at 1.31nm wavelength is presented and simulated successfully. The amplitude or intensity of digital modulation and demodulation of the chaotic ultra-wideband fiber communication are discussed.

articleTitle: Harmonic noise-like square pulse in an Er:Yb co-doped fiber laser at 1.61μm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The generation of high-power harmonic noise-like square pulses (NLSPs) is realized at 1.61 μm in an Er:Yb co-doped all-fiber mode-locked laser for the first time. By changing pump power and adjusting intra-cavity polarization state, the NLSP can operate in a fundamental or a high-order harmonic mode-locking (HML) state. The maximum average output power is about 1.26 W. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a watt-level harmonic NLSP.

articleTitle: Sensing Characteristics of Helical Long-Period Grating Inscribed in Graded Index Few Mode Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Helical long-period grating fabricated in graded-index few-mode fiber was experimentally demonstrated. The high sensitivities corresponding to torque, curvature, temperature and surrounding refractive index are up to 0.293 nm/rad/m, 2.486nm/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 0.095 nm/□ and 1242 nm/RIU, respectively.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg grating in seven core fiber fabricated with infrared femtosecond laser pulses and a phase mask
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fibre Bragg grating (FBG) is inscribed into a seven core optical fibre by use of femtosecond laser side illumination. Multiple peaks in the reflection and transmission spectrum are observed, which result from the Bragg resonance of the core mode and cladding mode by phase match condition. The grating spectra exhibit linear response to rising temperature, and a sensitivity of 12 pm/°C is achieved between room temperature and 1000°C. Such a Bragg grating is promising to find applications in harsh environments.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of etched physical structure fiber Bragg grating for fabricating high temperature sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Side-polishing single-mode fiber (SP-SMF) to the D-fiber and etch the physical structure Grating into the polishing flat surface. The simulation results of SP-SMF by COMSOL software show that the electric field contour lines at the air-cladding interface is continuous when the fiber cladding is polished to closer the core. Using Rsoft software to simulate the side-polished and etched fiber Bragg grating( SP-EFBG) and obtained the structural parameters of SP-EFBG, when the grating period and grating length and grating depth of the simulated SP-EFBG are 775nm and 10000μm and 150nm respectively, obtain the central wavelength and bandwidth and peak reflectivity is 1550nm and 0.2044nm and 90.79% respectively.

articleTitle: Research on the Gain Saturation Induced Noise in an Optical Fiber Sensing System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In an optical fiber sensing time division multiplexing (TDM) system, when the optical pulse with high peak power and low repetition rates is boost amplified, it is prone to be gain saturation and pulse distortion. The paper analysed their effects on the intensity and phase noises, and the results show that the pulse distortion induced noise is mainly down-converted relative intensity noise (RIN) lines spectra caused by the gain jitter. Then the RIN lines are converted into corresponding phase noise lines by the interferometer, which finally cause false signals in the sensor system. However in the case of saturated gain and pulse distortion, the increase of noise background is insignificant. Basing on the above results, several noise suppression schemes have been proposed, which will provide guidance for the design of large-scale remote sensing systems in the future.

articleTitle: Relative Intensity Noise Measurement of a Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Relative intensity noise (RIN) is used to characterize the temporal stability of a standard fiber laser. And the RIN spectra of an oscillator and a master oscillator power amplifier at same output power are compared.

articleTitle: Silicon/2D-materials Photonic Integrated Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Silicon photonics has attracted much attention because of the CMOS compatibility, high integrated density, etc. However, silicon is not a good option for active photonic integrated devices due to its indirect-bandgap structure. Recently, two-dimensional (2D) materials, such as graphene and black phosphorus (BP), exhibit excellent optical and electronic properties, and thus provide a potential option for realizing active photonic integrated devices on silicon. In this paper, we present our recent works on silicon/2D-materials photonic integrated devices for photodetection and thermal-tuning.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Mode-Locked Fiber Laser Emitting Scalar and Vector Noise-Like Pulses
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on a bidirectional nonlinear polarization rotation based mode-locked fiber laser emitting scalar and vector noise-like pulses in opposite directions. Furthermore, polarization resolved measurement is utilized to experimentally validate the vector noise-like pulses.

articleTitle: Experimental Assessment of Photonic Integrated Switches Based Optical Data Center Networks with Virtual Network Slice Services
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An SDN-controlled DCN based on photonic integrated switches is experimentally assessed. Network-slice can be reconfigured within 150 ms and deployed photonic integrated switches perform error-free 10 Gb/s switching with <; 2dB penalty and zero packet-loss.

articleTitle: Composite transparent conductive electrode for printed electronic devices
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The new transparent conductive electrode consists of three materials: silver nanowires (AgNWs), zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO), and reduced graphene oxide (rGO). We prepared a silver nanowire electrode by spin coating a silver nanowire solution on a glass substrate, the zinc oxide nanoparticles covered the silver nanowire grid and filled the gap of silver nanowire, which enhanced the adhesion of silver nanowire to the substrate. The outermost reduced graphene oxide provides protection for the material and improves the stability of the electrode in an air environment. The AgNWs/ZnO/rGO composite electrode prepared has a sheet resistance of about 9.96 Ω/sq and a light transmittance of 71% (T550), which has good photoelectric properties. Experimental results show that the composite electrode has long-term stability in air.

articleTitle: A closed micro-cavity in-fiber air pressure sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An air pressure sensor is demonstrated based on a closed micro-cavity F-P (Fabry-Perot) optical fiber interferent sensing structure. The interferent wavelengths present red-shift with the air pressure increase. Its sensing sensitivity can get 1.271nm/MPa for the linear fitting of the experiment results.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Materials Based on Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we apply THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) technique combined with gradient boosting decision tree algorithm to analyse the content of a-lactose in the lotus root starch mixture quantitatively. The terahertz absorption spectrum of a mixture of lotus root starch, a-lactose and polyethylene was measured by a THz-TDS system. Quantitative regression model of a-lactose content in the mixture was established by principal component regression (PCR), partial least squares regression (PLS), support vector regression (SVR) and gradient boosting regression (GBR). At the same time, the content of a-lactose in the mixture was obtained. The results show that the quantitative analysis of GBR model has higher accuracy and better fitting effect, and it will have broad development prospects and have the value of practical application in the field of quantitative analysis.

articleTitle: Superposition Construction of NB-QC-LDPC Codes for optical communication systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the construction of NB-QC-LDPC code in the framework of superposition for optical communication systems. By maximizing the girth and reducing the number of g-cycles of the base matrix, NB-QC-LDPC codes with good cycle distributions could be constructed. Simulation results show that, with the same implementation cost, the constructed codes could achieve 0.1dB~0.4dB NCG in iterative decoding at the BER of 10 when compared with the recent proposed codes.

articleTitle: Chaos in Frequency Domain using Multistable System with Fiber Michelson interferometer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Wavelength is used to induce optical nonlinearities and to generate chaos of multistable state from a tunable fiber laser with fiber Michelson interferometer (FMI). This laser is based on semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) and the fiber Fabry-Perot filter (FFP) used to tune continuous wavelength. PZT attended on FFP has longer response time and plays an important part in delay time. Chaos is realized by experiments and chaos behaviors are observed from oscillograph.

articleTitle: Design of a low-dispersion ring-core photonic crystal fiber supporting 26 OAM modes
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a new photonic crystal fiber structure to support 26 orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes from 1.25μm to 1.95μm. It has been proven that this fiber has good performance by the numerical analysis, such as low confinement loss, and relatively flat chromatic dispersion. The fiber has only two-layer of air holes, which makes it easier to be manufactured. What's more, the fiber has a more stable physical structure, the triangular arrangement of air holes which can guarantee the air holes hardly deforms.

articleTitle: Curvature Sensing Based On The Reflection Spectrum Of A Hybrid-Structure Fiber Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Simultaneous measurement of curvature and temperature by monitoring the transmission spectrum of a hybrid-structure fiber sensor which consists of two peanut-shape structures and a FBG is proposed in this paper. Besides the transmission spectrum, reflection spectrum of this hybrid-structure sensor can also be used for the curvature measurement. Unlike the wavelength demodulation of the transmission spectrum, the reflection spectrum which employs the intensity demodulation has an evident advantage that we can realize the measurement of curvature by using a relatively simple optical power meter instead of an elaborate and expensive OSA in practical application, which can reduce the cost well.

articleTitle: Research on real-time BER estimation in satellite downlink
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To overcome the disadvantage of BER measurement which must be tested in close loop with the source data foreknown, a online real time BER estimation method based on EVM which is analyzed in the prospect of signal quality is proposed, and a test system is built to simulate the satellite downlink. Experiments results show that the deviation between BER predicted and the measured is no more than 33%, which is acceptable in the BER test.

articleTitle: Soliton Self-Frequency Shift in Mode Locked Fiber Lasers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate the soliton evolution in a mode locked Er-doped fiber laser with intra-cavity soliton self-frequency shift by numerical simulation, and analyze the effects of different parameters including of pump strength, length of dispersion shift fiber (DSF), and modulation depth of saturable absorber in detail for the first time. The results show that once the stable output pulse is formed, the frequency shift amount would increase with increasing the pump strength or decreasing the length of DSF and the modulation depth.

articleTitle: Micro-displacement Sensor with Temperature Compensation based on Double-ball Cascade and Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: According to the double-ball structure and the sensing characteristics of the fiber Bragg grating (FBG), a micro-displacement sensor with temperature compensation is proposed and verified experimentally. The sensing structure is made of a FBG and a double-ball cascade. The first ball is used to excite the cladding mode, and the second can get the coupling interference between the cladding mode and the core mode. In the light of Bragg grating's inherent temperature characteristic, it can only be used to estimate temperature. The drift of single mode fiber interference dip and Bragg grating transmission spectrum are independent of each other. It reduces the influence of cross sensitivity between temperature and displacement. The experimental results show that the micro-displacement and temperature detection ranges are 0~0.16mm and 20~160°C; the micro-displacement and temperature sensitivities of the sensor are -89.892 nm/mm and -0.088 nm/°C, respectively. And the temperature sensitivity of FBG dip is 0.012 nm/°C. The micro-displacement measurement with temperature-compensated can be obtained by calculating the sensing matrix.

articleTitle: Dispersion-Managed Soliton Molecules in An All-Fiber Mode-Locked Fiber Laser With Near Zero Dispersion
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Characterized by particle-like behaviors, soliton molecules comprise abundant and interesting multi-soliton dynamics and further unveil vivid pulse-interaction scenarios towards the research community of ultrafast fiber lasers. Here, we report the formation of dispersion-managed solitons (DMSs) in an all-fiber laser passively mode-locked by a 45° tilted fiber grating (45° TFG) near the zero-dispersion regime. Particularly, typical DMS singlets are observed, possessing a broadband and smooth spectral shape. Besides, based on the reinforced stretching-compressing process during the pulse propagation, various multi-pulse DMS molecules are also discovered. Moreover, the transient soliton dynamics of dual-pulse and triple-pulse DMS molecules covering the timescale over hundreds of round trips are illustrated based on dispersive Fourier transformation (DFT) technique. The investigation of multi-soliton compounds, caused by direct soliton interaction, probably paves access to the explorations of nonlinear dynamics in mode-locked lasers.

articleTitle: Error Analysis of the Impulse Response on VCSEL-based Optical Wireless Communication Channel Using a Monte Carlo Ray-Tracing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article proposed a Monte Carlo ray-tracing method (MCRM) based on Gaussian beam emitter for optical wireless communication (OWC) channel estimation and established two typical indoor communication systems as uplink and full-link models. Formulas are given with targeted parameters for these two specific link models. The calculation results show that the impulse response of uplink models have twice larger and 10 ns faster than that of full-link models. Compared with the conventional Lambertian OWC systems, the Gaussian systems have larger impulse response and lower relative error, which indicates that Gaussian emitter is a promising candidate for indoor OWC system.

articleTitle: On-Line Collision Hazard Assessment for Fractionated Satellite Clusters with Proximity Relative Motion
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Given the characteristics of fractionated satellite clusters with proximity relative motion, a new on-line collision hazard assessment method based on performance parameters is presented that accounts for the navigation system, the collision-avoidance control capability and the communication performance of each module. Simulation results showed the efficiency resulting from its good adaptability, which benefits from the on-line self-adjusting enveloping solid adapting to different the encounter mode.

articleTitle: Analysis of core eccentricity on the long period grating in eccentric core fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The model of the long period fiber grating (LPFG) inscribed in the eccentric core fiber (ECF) is proposed and analyzed theoretically. The variation of the transmission spectrum is calculated under different eccentricities on the basis of the coupled-mode theory. The calculation results indicate that the order of the cladding mode that has the largest coupling efficient with the core mode changes with the change of the core eccentricity, which results in the shift of the resonant peaks. In addition, the effective refractive index of the fundamental mode increases with the core eccentricity within a certain range. The model we have proposed can provide a valid reference for designing ECF and writing LPFG in the ECF.

articleTitle: Uniform-Multilevel Amplitude Regeneration using a Polarization-orthogonal Continuous-wave-light-assisted Nonlinear-optical Loop Mirror
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally investigate a multilevel amplitude regeneration of NRZ-PAM4 signals using a novel polarization-orthogonal continuous-wave-light-assisted nonlinear-optical loop mirror (PC-NOLM) subsystem, which creates the uniform noise-suppression behavior on multiple amplitude levels.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Optimal Shaping Gain Selection MethodBased on Huffman Coding
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive optimal shaping gain selection method based on huffman coding is proposed. By nonuniform mapping, the input signal satisfies the optimal (secondary) distribution under different SNR, that is, the input signal is infinitely close to Maxwell Boltzmann distribution, so that the channel capacity wirelessly approaches the Shannon limit. The method not only improves the transmission performance of the system, increases the shaping gain, but also saves the algorithm complexity and system cost, and realizes the optimal distribution of the optimal (secondary)input signals under different SNR, thereby infinitely approaching the high-speed transmission of the channel capacity.

articleTitle: Time Delay Signature Suppression of Chaos in a Semiconductor Laser Subject to Feedback from Parallel-Coupled Triple Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically demonstrated a time delay signature suppressed chaos generation scheme by using external-cavity semiconductor laser subject to feedback from parallel-coupled triple ring resonator. Simultaneously, the effective bandwidth of chaos can be also extended obviously.

articleTitle: Dual-Parameter Modulation Leads to Chaos in An Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We study dual-parameter modulating how to lead to chaos in an erbium-doped fiber laser. When the pump and photon decay rate of the laser is modulated, a few paths to chaos are discussed.

articleTitle: A New Method for Measuring Laser Noise Based on Non-equilibrium Fiber Optic Interference System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new method is proposed to measure the intensity noise and phase noise of laser by using the natural drift of the working point of the non-equilibrium fiber optic interferometer.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-enhanced refractive index sensor based on series structure of two microfiber knot resonators with Vernier effect
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a sensor for sensitivity-enhanced refractive index (RI) sensing based on Vernier effect. The Vernier effect achieved by connecting two microfiber knot resonators (MKRs) in series. The sensing principles and spectrum of the structure are studied theoretically and then verified experimentally. The results exhibit that the RI sensor has high sensitivity up to 3301.76 nm/RIU and it is detection resolution is 6.057×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> RIU. That is because the microfiber has high proportional evanescent field and Vernier effect multiplies the spectrum of individual MKR. The proposed series structure of two MKRs with high sensitivity, easy fabrication and low cost can be extensively applied to physical, chemical and biological signal detection.

articleTitle: Gnss Passive Radar Imaging Based on Differential Aperture
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a passive imaging scheme with differential aperture based on multiple GNSS satellites and multiple ground receivers is studied. Firstly, the passive imaging model with differential aperture is established. Then, the factors affecting spatial imaging resolution are analysed. Finally, an inversion method based on point-by-point matched filtering technology is presented. It is seen that the diversity of aperture can be used to compensate for the shortage of narrow bandwidth of GNSS signal, so as to improve the overall spatial resolution of passive radar. Simulation results verify effectiveness of related analysis.

articleTitle: Hybrid-Cavity Semiconductor Lasers for Single Mode Operation And Optical Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Hybrid-cavity of a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity and a microcavity with the microcavity as a wavelength selective reflector are reported for realizing single mode semiconductor lasers. Mode coupling between a microcavity mode and a FP mode results in mode Q factor enhancement and stable single mode operation. Furthermore, optical bistability are realized in the hybrid lasers as the unbiased microcavity working as a saturable absorption. Two bistability regions are realized for the hybrid lasers around threshold current and above threshold with mode competition, and all-optical flip-flop is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband Reflector based on Subwavelength All-dielectric Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the design an ultra-broadband highly reflective subwavelength grating that covers almost the entire visible region. Results show that high reflectivity above 90% covering 450–700 nm can be achieved, corresponding to Δλ/λ=43%. We also provide intuitive physical insights into the broadband high reflection performance of reflector. We expect that this ultra-thin, ultra-broadband and highly reflective all-dielectric reflector can find applications in hyperspectral imaging based on tunable etalon filters.

articleTitle: Peanut-type fiber based hydrogen sensor coated by PDMS covered with WO3/SiO2
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A hydrogen sensor based on a peanut-type fiber coated with a film of PDMS covered with WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> hybird powder was proposed. Mach-Zehnder interferometer is composed of two peanut-type structures and a single-mode optical fiber. Two peanut-type surfaces were coated with PDMS films coated with WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/SIO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> powder. The proposed sensor has the sensitivity of 0.47db/% with a linear correlation of 98.3% in the concentration range of 0% - 0.901%.

articleTitle: Fiber optic planar accelerometer based on modal interferometer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber optic planar accelerometer for low frequency micro-vibration detection is proposed. The measured sensitivity, resolution and directional crosstalk are 227.82 mV/g, 12.54 μg/√Hz and -45.88 dB (8-100 Hz). The temperature crosstalk is -0.5 nm/°C.

articleTitle: THz-wave Signal Generation based on Optical Frequency Comb by One MZM
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel Terahertz-wave (THz-wave) signal generation based on optical frequency comb by only one single-drive MZM in 0.4 THz band by simulation. Bit-error-ratio (BER) curves of the QPSK and 16QAM signal proved feasible.

articleTitle: Black Phosphorus Based Ultrafast Yb-doped Fiber Laser: Principle, Mechanisms, and Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Since early 2014, black phosphorus (BP), a rising star among post-graphene, has been exploited to generate ultrashort pulses in fiber lasers. BP has a large direct bandgap range from 0.3 eV (bulk, corresponding to 4.13 μm) to 2 eV (monolayer, corresponding to 620 nm), which enables ultrashort pulse generation from near-infrared to visible waveband. In our progresses, an ultra-stable (more than 100 days) pulse fiber laser based on real BP-SA was demonstrated, which exhibited various interesting ultrafast phenomenon in 1 μm region. Our results extended the application of BP in the spatial and temporal domains.

articleTitle: Super-Multi-Junction Solar Cells, a New Configuration of the Robust and High-Efficiency Solar Cell and Its Application – Operation Model Based on the Annual Monitoring of the Multi-Junction PV Modules
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: It is known that multi-junction solar cells are sensitive to the spectrum change [1]-[2], and its high-performance is often discouraged by the spectrum mismatching loss by the seasonal change of the atmospheric parameters [3]-[4]. It implies that the highest efficiency solar cell in the standard testing condition does not always promise the most excellent annual energy yield in the real world solar condition that the spectrum is ever-changing. We found the ultimate solution of the seasonal loss will be autonomous compensation of the carrier imbalance by the radiative coupling among junctions due to radiative recombination [5]. We call it a super-multi-junction solar cell. The annual operation of the super-multi-junction solar cell was simulated by the validated operation model of the photovoltaic module using multi-junction solar cells. It was shown that the super-multi-junction architecture was found robust up to 6 junctions. The robust high-efficiency solar cell can be the right candidate of the vehicle-integrated photovoltaic that run a majority of electric vehicles on solar energy.

articleTitle: The Study of Data Processing System for the FBG Temperature Sensor Network Based on the Hadoop Platform
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A large-scale network of fiber Bragg grating (FBG) temperature sensors can detect ambient temperature field information. But mass data acquisition and real-time analysis of temperature data are very difficult, where can paralyze some sensor network nodes. So the processing of the big data has brought challenge to data processing system, the emergence of the cloud computing brings back to life for the storage and processing of big data. In this paper, a data processing system is built with the Hadoop, the HBase and the JSP, which is an open source framework used widely. The design of the data processing system provides a basic platform to the big data for FBG temperature sensor network, and it has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Design Of A New Thresholder Using For Spiking Photonic Neuron
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an ultrafast spiking photonic neuron is illustrated with a new thresholder that based on a designed Sagnac loop. The novel all-optical thresholder (AOT) is internally passive with unified outside pump source in a highly nonlinear of hollow-core photonic crystal fiber(HC-PCF) loop. It can eliminate noise accumulation and results in robust and efficient information processing and achieves a high extinction ratio in our simulation. This neuron works in a low power state.

articleTitle: A novel polarization-insensitive optical filter on silicon
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A silicon-based polarization-insensitive optical filter is designed and demonstrated by using dual multimode-waveguide-gratings. For the ~300μm-long device, the 3dB-bandwidth is ~11nm and the excess loss is ~1.5dB for both polarizations.

articleTitle: New mechanism Vernier Effect to amplify the sensitivity based on separated Fabry-perot interferometers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new method to amplify the sensitivity based on separated Fabry-perot interferometers (FPI) causing Vernier effect is presented and discussed. The spectrum of typical cascaded cavity based on Vernier effect is analyzed and simulated. We also propose a novel structure to realize Vernier effect to amplify the sensitivity, using two separated FPI. The simulation shows that the disturbance term in the spectrum is eliminated, and sensitivity is the same as cascaded cavities'.

articleTitle: Improvement of soliton pulse energy in thulium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we report a thulium-doped fiber based on nonlinear polarization rotation technology. Increasing the pump power to 600mW and adjusting the polarization controllers, Gaussian pulse with high pulse energy can be achieved. The pulse duration of de-chirped pulse is 553 fs. Due to dispersion management, excessive nonlinear phase shift accumulation can be avoided. The maximum output power of the resonant cavity is 86.3mW, and the corresponding pulse energy is 2.96nJ.

articleTitle: An MMF-NCF-MMF Structure Based SPR Sensor for Highly Sensitive Detection of Glucose and Salt Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optic-fiber SPR sensor based on no-core fiber (NCF) is presented and available for microfluidic chip. Our sensor has advantages of high sensitivity (3094 nm / RIU), wide RI range (1.333-1.405) and compactness.

articleTitle: Tunable Microwave Photonic Filter with Negative and Complex Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Tunable microwave photonic filter (MPF) with negative and complex coefficients is proposed and demonstrated. The multiple wavelengths optical source with stability and flatness can be realized by using a broadband source (BBS) and a waveshaper1. The negative coefficients of the MPF can be implemented by an electroopic polarization modulator (PoIM), and the cut-off frequency response can be effectively eliminated. The amplitude and phase of the optical carriers and phase modulation sidebands can be controlled by Fourier domain optical processor (FD-OP), which the complex coefficient and tunability of the MPF can be realized. In the experiment, the 10 taps with 0.2nm are used as input optical source, the free spectrum range (FSR) is 34.91GHz. The center frequency is continuously tuned from 0 to 34.97 GHz and the shape remains unchanged.

articleTitle: 0.5 mm resolution distributed fiber strain sensor with a location-deviation compensation algorithm based on OFDR
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a 0.5mm spatial resolution distributed fibre strain sensor with a location-deviation compensation algorithm based on Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry. This algorithm compensates for spatial location-deviation of the sensor and degenerated correlation of the Rayleigh spectra. Experimental results reveal a 0.5 mm spatial resolution at the 25 m fibre end, with 50000 equivalent sensors. The strain accuracy of ±15με is achieved in ±2500με using a polyimide-coated fibre. The distributed fiber sensor provides practical use in sensing applications.

articleTitle: A Poldemux Scheme Using Extended Kalman Filter in Probabilistic Shaping Stokes Vector Direct Detection System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a Kalman filter based PolDemux scheme to cope with probabilistically shaped 16QAM signals in Stokes vector direct detection system. It can track the SOP variation up to 2Mrad/s at a relative lower OSNR.

articleTitle: An all-optical sampling system utilizing QD-SOA-based NOLM
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an all-optical sampling system. The ring-shaped mode-locked laser with quantum-dot semiconductor optical amplifier (QD-SOA) is the sampling pulse source of the system. The sampling module consists of a Nonlinear Optical Loop Mirror (NOLM) utilizing QD-SOA as the nonlinear element. Simulation results show that the high-frequency narrow Gaussian pulse of 40 GHz can optically sample the 4 GHz dual-frequency Gaussian pulse signal. The system has the advantages of fast sampling speed and high sampling accuracy.

articleTitle: New Interpolation Method for Shape Sensors Based on Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an improved method to reconstruct object shape for shape sensors based on fiber bragg grating (FBG), where FBG array is embedded in silicone gel as protection shell and glued on rubber tape surface to distinguish bending direction. The calibration experiments of FBG are presented to ensure relative precise conversion between FBG wavelength offsets and bending curvature. In the improved method, spline interpolation technique instead of traditional linear technique is employed to characterize relationship between bending curvature and arc length, with Frenet-serret equation used in the procedure of object shape reconstruction. The experiment results show that spline interpolation technique induces lower error than linear interpolation technique, which verifies that an improvement in object shape reconstruction can be achieved by employing spline interpolation technique.

articleTitle: Two-mode multiplexer based on the multilayer Si-SiN platform for 2μm waveband
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated a two-mode multiplexer in the multi-layer Si-SiN platform for 2um waveband. The insertion loss of the mode multiplexer link is less than 2.2 dB across the wavelength 1945 nm-1985 nm.

articleTitle: Graphene-based Hybrid Plasmonic Modulator with High Modulation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A graphene-based hybrid plasmonic modulator (GHPM) is proposed by adopting the electro-absorption effect of graphene. The simulation results show that the modulation efficiency of GHPM can be as large as 0.417 dB/μm, which is more than twice as much as that of recently presented graphene-on-silicon modulator (GOSM). Then we fabricate a prototype of GHPM. The measurement results demonstrate that the GHPM can work in a broadband from 1530 nm to 1570 nm and an improved modulation efficiency of 1.08 dB (at 30 μm). At last, we have discussed the factors that influence the modulation efficiency. Our work may promote the development of on-chip graphene-based plasmonic devices.

articleTitle: Application of Micro-Nano Grating in Photonic Regulation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Micro-nano gratings have become an important research direction of integrated optics because of its simple structure, easy integration, and multi-functionality. This paper introduces the research status of micro-nano gratings in the field of photon regulation, and provides reference for the development of the industry.

articleTitle: A High-selectivity Photonic Lantern Demultiplexer for Weakly-coupled Mode Group Demultiplexing over MMF
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a high-selectivity photonic lantern demultiplexer for weakly-coupled mode group demultiplexing over MMF. The simulated mode-group demultiplexer shows a mode-group selectivity higher than 28.2 dB for all 3 mode groups over the C-band.

articleTitle: A Temperature Sensing Scheme Realized with Sagnac Interferometer Based Microwave Photonic Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a temperature sensing scheme realized with Sagnac interferometer (SI) based microwave photonic filter (MPF) has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated. In our experiment, the sensitivities of -1.6 MHz/°C and -1.29 MHz/°C have been achieved by using SI with the length of polarization maintaining fiber (PMF) of 7.3 m and 5.3 m acting as the sensing fiber, respectively. The proposed sensing scheme converts the wavelength spacing changes of the SI to the frequency shifts of the MPF's passband, and thus has an unlimited measurement range.

articleTitle: Monitoring ammonia through cavity-enhanced absorption spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on near infrared cavity-enhanced absorption spectroscopy (CEAS), we develop an optical off-axis enhanced cavity sensor system for ammonia monitoring. A tunable DFB laser scanned around 1510.44nm is used to probe absorption spectrum of ammonia gas at a vacuum pressure of 25kPa. Traceable standard ammonia gas is injected into the sensor system cavity at a gas flow of 600ml/min to calibrate the sensor system. And then the linearity and sensitivity of the sensor system are investigated for ammonia at the same working conditions. Maximum measuring error of only is achieved ranging from 0 to 1000 ppm, showing a higher performance for ammonia gas detection than traditional commercial electrochemical sensor systems. It offers a combination of sensitivity, robustness, dynamic range and easy operation in practical application.

articleTitle: Structure Colors Realized by TiN-Si3N4-Si Nanostructure Array
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a nanostructure array is proposed to achieve a full-wavelength structural color in the visible range. The nanostructure is designed in form of triangular prism which is composed of three layers of TiN, Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and Si materials. The cross section of the triangular prism is an isosceles triangle. By calculating the reflectance of such nanostructure array, it is found that the periodic variation has little effect on the scattering peak of the nanostructure array when we vary the cross-sectional area of the triangular prism and the period respectively. As the cross-sectional area of the triangular prism increases, the scattering peak shifts to red. According to our simulation, a variety of colors such as purple, green, cyan, orange, and red can be obtained. The proposed nanostructure array, which utilizes TiN as capping layer, can provide some new ways for realizing a sustainable structural color for various applications.

articleTitle: Microfiber Controlled Wavelength-tunable Mode-locked Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser using Carbon Nanotube Polymer Film
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a wavelength-tunable passively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser based on carbon nanotube and intermodal interference of the microfiber. Continuously tuning range from 1569.6 nm to 1561.57 nm is achieved under single pulse operation.

articleTitle: Edge-coupled III-V/Si3N4 hybrid external cavity laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated an III-V/silicon nitride hybrid external cavity laser (ECL). The ECL exhibits a tuning range of 45 nm, a side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of 60 dB, and a linewidth of round 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Multi-points ultrasound detection with multiple FBGs and a pseudo-synchronous method
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel pseudo-synchronous method(PSM)is proposed to realize the multi-points detection of ultrasound with fiber Bragg sensors (FBGs) connected in serials, to overcome the problems encountered by employing conventional wavelength demodulator for FBGs at relatively low repeat frequency(~1kHz), comparing with the much higher frequency up to several tens of kHz of the ultrasound to be detected. The novel detection scheme has been demonstrated effectively when the ultrasound was excited and propagating on the surfaces of an aluminium plate and a section of stainless steel tube, respectively. The experimental measurement shows the detection method has good prospect in practical application such as the non-destructive test (NDT), etc.

articleTitle: Analysis on Gain And Noise Figure of Direct Modulation RoF Link
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The equivalent circuit model of direct modulation RoF link is introduced. Based on this model, the mathematical expressions of link gain and noise figure are both derived. The factors affecting the transmission characteristics, especially the parasitic parameters of lasers and detectors, are further analyzed. Finally, a general method to improve link gain and reduce noise figure is given.

articleTitle: Large-range Dynamic Strain Measurement Using Chaotic BOCDA
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a wide-range dynamic strain measurement system using single-slope assisted chaotic BOCDA. In SBS-based chaotic sensors, the linewidth of chaotic BGS is naturally broaden due to the multi-frequency pump wave. Thus, the linear section is provided a large dynamic range. This experiment is the first that a dynamic strain of 1200 με can be accurately identified using the single-slope assisted method, which is a significant improvement. The proposed method has a great demand potential in large-scale dynamic strain measurement.

articleTitle: Polymer/Silica Hybrid Three-Dimension Integrated Multiplexer Based on MDM and WDM
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a polymer/silica hybrid three-dimension integrated multiplexer based on mode division multiplexing (MDM) and wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) is proposed. WDM is implemented on different layers by two multimode interference (MMI) couplers, and MDM is achieved by a three-dimension integrated asymmetric directional coupler (ADC). The directional coupling between the fundamental mode in the silica waveguide and the first-order mode in the polymer waveguide is realized by three-dimension integration of the upper polymer waveguide and the lower silica waveguide, and the WDM of 1310nm and 1550nm wavelength channels is realized by using structurally compact MMI coupler. The integration density of the chip is improved by multi-material hybrid integration and three-dimension integration, and the transmission capacity of the chip is increased by the multifunction integration of MDM and WDM.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Mixed Lead-Tin Halide Perovskites for Visble Light-Emitting Diodes
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Lead halide perovskites as a new generation of outstanding semiconductor materials have attracted considerable attention. The excellent optical properties and emission qualities makes this kind of materials suitable for light emitting diodes (LED). However, the toxicity of lead limits its large-scale industrial production. Here, we report the gradual reduction of lead content in two-dimensional perovskites by substituting lead with non-toxic tin for preparation of two-dimensional perovskites light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) with different tin-lead ratios. Among these devices, the lead-free PeLEDs exhibits electroluminescence at 615 nm with peak luminance of 117 cd/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 0.18%.

articleTitle: Aminopeptidase N (CD13) Modified Gold Films for the Affinity Quantitative Detection of CNGRC-coupled Derivative
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article proposes a fiber optic SPR sensor system for quantitative detection of APN-targeting ligand CNGRC-coupled derivative, and obtained a lower limit of detection determined to be 0.22 fg/ml.

articleTitle: Tunable Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser Assisted by a fs-laser Introduced Random Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A tunable erbium-doped fiber (EDF) laser assisted by a random fiber grating introduced by an fs-laser and a tunable fiber Bragg grating is demonstrated. The tuning range is up to 4.45 nm( 1548.04 -1552.49 nm). Due to the half-opened laser cavity design and the efficient gain from the pumped EDF, the measured threshold pump power is 18 mW, and the slope efficiency is up to 13.2%.

articleTitle: Research on Fabrication Method of High Stability Long Period Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Long-period fiber gratings (LPFG )is sensitive to the changes of external parameters such as refractive index, temperature, bending, etc. Therefore, more stable writing of LPFG to obtain better performance is very important for the subsequent research of LPFG in optical fiber sensing. In this paper, on the basis of the research on the current LPFG writing method, a new method of LPFG writing with fiber fixation in the prestressed state is proposed, and the writing performance of LPFG in the multiple groups of prestressed state is compared through experiments. The results show that the proposed method has a better effect of writing stability, deeper modulation depth and narrower bandwidth.

articleTitle: Research of all-optical broadcast UWB pulse shape modulation signals based on semiconductor fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel scheme for all-optical generate ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse shape modulation (PSM) signals based on semiconductor fiber ring laser (SFRL) is proposed, in which three UWB PSM signals can be generated simultaneously. A comprehensive broad-band dynamic model of this kind of all-optical UWB PSM signals is presented and simulated. The numerical simulation results show that the central frequency (CF) of PSM signals, the -10dB bandwidth of PSM signals and the fractional bandwidth of PSM signals are 5GHz, 7GHz and 140%, respectively, which satisfy the definition of the UWB.

articleTitle: Optimization of Dead Time in SPAD-based Photon-Counting Communication System with Afterpulsing
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Afterpulsing is a critical non-ideal factor of single photon avalanche diode (SPAD) at telecommunication wavelength, which limits its performance. In order to optimize the dead time in SPAD operation, a multiple exponential model of afterpulsing probability (AP) is built and fitted with the testing data of QCD-300 single photon detector. Furthermore, a new bit error rate (BER) model of photon-counting communication system with afterpulsing is studied. Based on the joint model of AP and BER, the optimization of dead time in different bit times and background photon levels is investigated. The results indicate that the optimal dead time is constant with the variation of bit time. When background photon level increases, the optimal dead time will be increased quickly. And keeping the background photon level below 0.5-c/ns, the optimal dead time is below 32-ns.

articleTitle: Novel Four-Level Manchester Coding Technique for Optical Access Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Four-level Manchester coding (4-MC) technique investigated for high-speed optical access networks. Results show that 4-MC has 3.5dB better receiver sensitivity compared to 4-PAM, which makes 4-MC an alternative to 4-PAM together with self-clocking feature advantage.

articleTitle: Multipoint temperature sensor based on PDMS-filled Fabry Perot interferometer with an Array-Waveguide Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a multipoint temperature sensor based on Fabry Perot interferometer (FPI) with an array- waveguide grating (AWG) is proposed. The FPI is formed by welding a section of hollow core fiber (HCF) to the end of single mode fiber (SMF), and filling with PDMS polymer in the HCF. The AWG is used as a multiplexing and demultiplexing unit. The experimental results show that the proposed sensor has good performance. The average sensitivity of the three channels is -0.854dB/°C in the temperature range from 30°C to 40°C.

articleTitle: An optofluidic microcapillary biosensor for label-free, low glucose concentration detection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A microcapillary with a Q factor of 1.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and a 2-μm wall thickness is functionalized to detect glucose concentration of 2.78 mM, with sensitivity of 0.974 pm/mM and small sample volume ~ 90 nL.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive Microfiber Refractive Index Sensor Based on Mach-Zehnder Interference of Core Offset Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultrasensitive microfiber refractive index (RI) sensor was proposed and demonstrated based on the core offset Mach-Zehnder interference (MZI) fiber structure. It consisted of a core offset single-mode fiber (SMF) fusion spliced between two SMFs, where the center SMF was tapered to diameter of few micrometers. The experimental results showed that the sensor exhibits an ultrahigh RI sensitivity of 16485 nm /RIU (RI unit) within the RI range between 1.410 and 1.413 where the core offset and tapered fiber diameter were 7.5 μm and 9 μm, respectively. This proposed fiber sensor has the great potential as a base for biosensor in applications of air pollution monitoring, chemical elements detection and medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: The Effects of Laser Polarization on The Performance of Terahertz Time-domain Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber-type terahertz time-domain spectrometer was designed by combining fiber femtosecond laser with fiber-coupled photoconductive antenna. The effects of laser polarization on the terahertz time-domain waveform, intensity and spectral characteristics are studied experimentally. By precise control and optimization of the polarization state of the femtosecond laser, the time-domain pulse splitting phenomenon is eliminated, and a single peak time-domain pulse with high signal-to-noise ratio is obtained.

articleTitle: A Passively Mode-locked Tm-doped Fiber Laser Based on PbS Nanoparticles as Saturable Absorber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A passively mode-locked Tm-doped fiber laser was experimentally achieved by using PbS nanoparticles as a saturable absorber (SA), for the first time. The laser delivers stable conventional solitons with pulse duration of 1.24 ps at the repetition rate of 21.93 MHz. The centered wavelength and 3-dB bandwidth are 1957.37 nm and 3.43 nm, respectively. The high signal noise ratio of 61 dB indicates the good stability of the mode-locking. By further increasing pump power, the laser switches into stable second harmonic mode-locked regime. In this state, the average output power of 9.06 mW and repetition rate of 43.86 MHz are obtained. The results reveal that PbS is a type of promising SA for 2 μm ultra-short pulse generation.

articleTitle: SSB Modulation With Optimum Optical Carrier to Sideband Ratio Based on Polarization modulated Optical Signal Injected Into DFB Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel approach to perform a single sideband (SSB) modulation signal with optimum carrier to sideband ratio (OCSR) of 0 dB based on polarization modulated optical signal injected into DFB laser is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. When the polarization modulated optical signal is injected into DFB laser, due to the frequency selective gain feature of optical injected DFB laser, one sideband is amplified while the optical carrier and the other sideband are not changed. Therefore, the SSB signal is obtained. Adjusting polarization control (PC) to change the OCSR and obtain the SSB modulation with OCSR 0 dB and the amplitude difference of 44.87 dB.

articleTitle: Mode manipulation based on few-mode fiber devices
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, several kinds of few-mode fiber (FMF) based devices has been designed. Then an all-FMF mode-locked ring laser with carbon nanotubes was demonstrated with the generation of high purity cylindrical vector beams (CVBs).

articleTitle: Improved spectral performance of fiber sensor using Brillouin slow light
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design a scheme that the spectral performance of a sensor can be improved by introducing a Brillouin slow light into it. The experimental results show that spectral sensitivity is enhanced by about 1.145 time.

articleTitle: Exciton tunneling behaviors in two dimensional halide perovskite
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskite materials have attracted great attention because of their impressive optoelectronic properties in light-emitting diodes (LED), sensors and solar cells, etc. Recently, it has been shown that the low dimensional perovskites with direct white light emission may act as the single component phosphors in next generation white-LEDs. Here, we demonstrate the temperature dependent photoluminescence (PL) properties of white light 2D perovskites by laser excitation. Spectroscopic measurements suggest that the white light spectrum consist of free exciton (FE) and self-trapped exciton (STE). The relative intensities between the FE and STE are temperature dependent, and the energy tunneling effect is dominated at low temperature while the thermal quenching is responsible for the higher temperature region. Our results give the physical insight of the energy transfer and thermal behaviours of the excitons in 2D perovskites.

articleTitle: Cascade Co-pumping – From a Comparison View
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, cascade co-pumping Erbium/Ytterbium codoped fiber lasers (EYDFLs) are studied from a comparison view. A 976 nm pumped EYDFL with a 1018 nm auxiliary cavity are compared with EYDFLs cladding-pumped at 915 nm, 940 nm, and core-pumped at 1018 nm, respectively, in aspects as optimal fiber length, pump conversion efficiency, thermal effects, and Yb ASE suppression. The results show that cascade co-pumping is the most effective method among these cases in efficiency, stability, compactness, and cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Application of ultra-stable laser in coherent optical frequency transfer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate the effect of utralstable laser in the high-precision coherent phase transfer of optical frequency. The ultra-stable laser with a linewidth of 0.68 Hz is applied for the optical frequency transfer over a 100 km-fiber link, achieving a transfer instability of 4.9× 10-17 at 100 s, which is about one order of magnitude superior than that with a 2.7 kHz linewidth laser, two times less than that with a 50 Hz linewidth laser. This indicates that the ultrastable lasers will play an important role in the optical frequency transfer.

articleTitle: In vivo and online temperature monitoring based on fiber Bragg greatings during tumor treatment with nanosecond pulse electric field
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensing system was used to online monitor the temperature at the surface of / inside the liver tissue of a rabbit under nanosecond pulse electric field (nsPEF). Single point measurement between the electrodes and multi-point measurement surrounding one electrode were both carried out. Experimental results show that, due to equally spaced (Δt=0.5 s) 300 ns-pulses with E=20 kV/cm at a repetition rate of 4 Hz, the temperature rise in the rabbit liver tumor usually does not exceed ΔT=6°C for 300 pulses. Theoretical analysis of Joule heating model fits well with the experimental results. Both direct measurements and theoretical modelling demonstrated that nsPEF could not deliver enough energy to heat the treated tissue significantly, thus a hyperthermic effect on the tissue can be excluded during this kind of treatment with much high electric field strength and extremely short duration.

articleTitle: 100 MHz Reconfigurable Ultrafast Swept Source by Time Stretching of 100 nm Flat-top Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The repetition rate of swept source determines the acquisition rate of optical coherence tomography and interrogation rate of optical sensing systems. The axial resolution of optical coherence tomography is limited by the swept range of the swept source. In this paper, we report an ultrafast time stretching swept source with up to 100 MHz repetition rate and a 100 nm flattop spectrum. The repetition rate can be reconfigured by incorporating with an optical modulator.

articleTitle: Deep Learning assisted Visible Light Communication based Intelligent Transport System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To reduce the incidence of traffic accidents, Visible Light Communication (VLC) based Intelligent Transport System (ITS) has been widely accepted as a promising solution. The Deep Learning technology can be utilized to help VLC based ITS applications both for vehicles and infrastructures. This paper proposes a deep learning assisted VLC unmanned vehicles which can automatically capture and identify different traffic signs. Then deep learning algorithm will be implemented and control the unmanned vehicle performing corresponding motion operations. Theoretical analysis and demo system are provided to verify the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Non-volatile silicon photonic devices enabled by phase change material
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We review our recent research progress on silicon-Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Te<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> hybrid photonic devices. The optical transmission can be varied by 20 dB using micron-length GST. The inherent "self-holding" feature of GST make it attractive for low-power applications.

articleTitle: Unraveling the Moisture-induced Decomposition Mechanism of Red-Emitting Perovskite CsPbBrI2 Nanocrystals and Enhancing their Stability through Copper(II) Substitution
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The implementation of red-Emitting perovskite CsPb(Br<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (0<; x<; 1) nanocrystals (NCs) is hindered because of their low structural stability, and the moisture-induced degradation pathways of these red-Emitting perovskite are not well-defined. In the present work, we show that the moisture-induced degradation of CsPbBrI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> NCs spontaneously forms CsPbBr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (α) and CsPbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(δ) and other decomposition products. On the other hand, highly stable and luminescent red perovskite CsPbBrI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> NCs were achieved through copper substitution and halide rich passivation strategy. We demonstrated that the incorporation of Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions can enhance formation energy, causing a slight lattice contraction, and hence stabilize the cubic phase of these NCs. Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>-substituted CsPbBrI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> NCs with higher luminescence were synthesized in a halide-rich passivation method. The highly stable and luminescent Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>-substituted CsPbBrI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> NCs can function well as efficient light emitters toward the fabrication of high-performance red perovskite LEDs.

articleTitle: Study of Infrared Image Denoising Algorithm Based on Steering Kernel Regression Image Guided Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Infrared image has the disadvantages of narrow dynamic range, low contrast and easy to be polluted by noise. For this reason, this paper proposes a new infrared image denoising method based on steering kernel regression image guided filter. In this method, the shape and size of the steering kernel are firstly determined according to the local gradient information of the image, and then the filtering weight is obtained by the steering kernel regression, which is used to modify the analysis window of image guided filtering. The experimental results show that the proposed method is better than the guided filter and the steering kernel regression algorithm. Compared with the traditional infrared image denoising algorithm, this method can retain the image details, and acquire better visual experience.

articleTitle: Image Registration SIFT Algorithm Based on Adaptive Adjustment of Grayscale Weight
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In view of the low color contrast of the foreground in the image of aero-engine blades, this paper optimizes the SIFT algorithm which was commonly used in image registration. The SSIM index and FSIM index in the image similarity evaluation standard are added to calculate. Using the ESFS index as the judgment standard for analysing the similarity between the color image and the corresponding grayscale image. To calculate a weight ratio which is better than the traditional algorithm. Experiments show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the traditional algorithm in saving the blade images ' information, and can acquire more feature point pairs in the subsequent SIFT registration process.

articleTitle: LOOP: A Low-Loss Compact Plasmonic Router for ONoC
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Silicon-based plasmonics has shown the potential to build an ideal optical router for optical Network-on-Chip. Simply replacing switching elements by plasmonic switches cannot fully utilize excellent properties of plasmonics. In this paper, we propose LOOP: a low-loss compact plasmonic router for mesh network. By adopting new topology, unique shape and high operation frequency of plasmonic devices are finely tuned to high-performance optical switching. Compared with other structures, LOOP shows lower insertion loss and utterly small footprint.

articleTitle: All-fiber Mode Acousto-optic Modulator in Gas Absorption Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper mainly studies the application of tunable laser and acoustic grating in TDLAS gas sensoring. The tunable laser is used for wavelength tuning, and the acoustic-vibration grating is used for signal light modulation in the TDLAS system. The ammonia harmonic signal detection at 1512.84 nm is realized. The feasibility of the tunable laser and the acoustic-vibration grating for ammonia detection is verified. The characteristics of the acoustic-vibration grating near 1512 nm are studied.
