articleTitle: Ambient Light Suppressed Free Space Optical Communication System based on FADOF
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a wireless optical communication system based on Faraday anomalous dispersion optical filter (FADOF) is proposed to suppress the ambient light. Experimental results show that the Q factor of 20Mbit/s OFDM-QPSK signal can be improved by 9 dB after filtering the ambient light by using the FADOF.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Communication Data Quality Analysis Software System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the design method of communication data quality analysis software based on Linux system, and implements the software under Qt environment. The software can automatically analyze the communication data generated by the ocean-going survey ship. It can automatically check the abnormal situation of communication data (including re-frame and frame loss) and identify the abnormal situation according to the content transcribed by users' needs. It can also provide the drawing function of specified format data and the auxiliary function of data analysis. The application results show that the data quality analysis software system can meet the daily use needs, greatly reduce the time of manual data analysis and improve the accuracy of the results.

articleTitle: An improvement on the CNN-based OAM Demodulator via Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In the paper, an Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) demodulation method based on Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks(CGAN) is proposed to improve the accuracy of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) based demodulator. We train a CGAN on a limited data set, and the discriminator in CGAN is fine-tuned as a new classifier for OAM demodulation. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method can improve the accuracy of OAM demodulator from 93.56% to 98.36% over 400-m free-space link when the turbulence strength C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> equals 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2/3</sup>.

articleTitle: High Power-Efficient 4D Trellis Coded Modulation PS-8PSK for Long-Haul Optical System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization-switched QPSK (PS-QPSK) based four-dimensional trellis coded modulation polarization-switched 8PSK (4DTCM-PS-8PSK) format with unparalleled superiority of low decoding complexity and high energy efficiency is proposed for the first time, which improves the bit-error-rate (BER) performance of PS-QPSK. The BER performance of 4DTCM-PS-8PSK is simulated. Simulation results indicates that 0.6 dB and 2.6 dB gains are obtained in the BER of 1.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> when comparing with the traditional PS-QPSK and dual-polarization QPSK(DP-QPSK), respectively. And the coding gain can be further enhanced with the increase of signal-to-noise ratio(SNR). Therefore, the favorable performance in sensitivity reveals the proposed 4DTCM-PS-8PSK can be of great potential for long-haul optical transmission systems at the cost of few extra complexities.

articleTitle: Sensitive detection of humidity based on tilted fiber Bragg grating coated with Graphene oxide and multi-walled carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A functionalized tilted fiber grating (TFBG) sensor based on graphene oxide (GO) and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MNCNT) was proposed for the detection of environmental relative humidity (RH). GO-MWCNT composites were coated on the surface of TFBG by heating deposition. Environmental humidity detection through the TFBG cladding mode resonance peak changes. The test results show that the relative humidity (RH) detection range is 30%-90%, the maximum sensitivity is 0.32/%RH. Furthermore, the proposed humidity sensor exhibits good performance in terms of repeatability and stability

articleTitle: Network Nervous System: When Multilayer Telemetry Meets AI-assisted Service Provisioning : (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a network nervous system (NNS) that leverages hybrid centralized/distributed processing to achieve automatic and effective network control and management (NC&M) for realizing artificial intelligence (AI) assisted service provisioning in IP over elastic optical networks (IPoEONs).

articleTitle: Coherent Optical Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing with Index Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: CO-OFDM with index modulation is proposed in this paper. Compared with the conventional CO-OFDM systems, the proposed scheme can improve spectral efficiency up to 6.25% with similar transmission performance.

articleTitle: A Miniature Near-infrared Spectrometer Based on Linear Variable Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A miniature near-infrared spectrometer based on Linear Variable Filter (LVF) was developed. The optical path and optics parameters of the spectrometer was optimized by Lighttools, and SolidWorks was used to model the spectrometer. The working wavelength range of the spectrometer is 970nm-1630nm, the resolution of the miniature near-infrared spectrometer at the central wavelength is 15nm, the diameter is 71mm, and the length is 76mm. We used the laser with wavelength of 1310nm and 1490nm as the light source to test the resolution of the miniature near-infrared spectrometer. Finally, we obtained the absorbance curve of water by testing filter papers of different humidity.

articleTitle: Polarization Sensitivity of Silicon Integrated Optical Antenna for Laser Communication on Small Satellite
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An integrated optical antenna is proposed for laser communication on the small satellite in which there are not enough internal space for large laser communication system. The proposed optical antenna is designed on a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) chip with two different grating couplers to receive and transmit the TE and TM modes respectively. The polarization angle of the incident light can be precisely measured by this optical antenna. The factors which cause the polarization angle errors are analyzed in detail. It is demonstrated that the measurement error for the polarization angle is less than 0.001° when the incident angle error is less than 0.008°. The optical antenna is sensitive to polarization angle and convenient to be installed on the surface of the carrier, providing a new approach for laser communication on the small satellite.

articleTitle: A 375Mb/s Real-time Internet of Vehicles System Based on Automotive Headlight Utilizing OFDM-64QAM Modulation Format
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a real-time Internet of Vehicles system based on an automotive headlight. The modulation format is OFDM-64QAM and we successfully reach the data rate of 375Mb/s by utilizing a FPGA as the central host. The transmission distance is 2.5m. We also investigated the performance of the system by calculating BER versus bias current, transmission distance and attenuation at both transmitter and receiver. As far as we know, this is the highest data rate of a real-time visible light communication system based on automotive headlight which can be used in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV).

articleTitle: Highly sensitive refractive index sensor with fiber in-line Fabry-Perot interferometers based on vernier effect
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A highly sensitive refractive index (RI) sensor with fiber in-line Fabry-Perot interferometers based on vernier effect is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The sensor is fabricated by splicing a short segment of capillary to a commercial single mode fiber (SMF) and then splicing a tiny large mode area fiber to the capillary. There are two micro-channels in the lateral wall of the tube. The sensor exhibits a compact size of less than 1 mm in total length and has the highest RI sensitivity of ~10189.2 nm/RIU within the range of 1.32846 to 1.33327.

articleTitle: A Fiber-Optic Channel Modeled Through BiLSTM Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we model the fiber-optic channel with bidirtectional LSTM struture, which shows the similar performance with the conventional method, while greatly reduced the need for expert konwledge and complexity.

articleTitle: Atomic Layered 2d/3d Heterostructure for Sensitive Photodetection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In recent years, there have been increasing interests in 2D materials, as a result of its outstanding basic properties and enormous potentiality of applications in photoelectric devices. In this work, a vertical 2D-GaSe/3D-GaSb heterostructure was fabricated by epitaxial growth and the device exhibits good photosensitivity and fast response speed of microsecond, which reveals a promising candidate for intergenerational development of photodetector.

articleTitle: Quantum-dot light-emitting diodes with NiO and NiO:Mg as hole injection layer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLED) have attracted great attention due to their impressive optoelectronic properties and stability. The most common used hole injection layer (HIL) material Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxytiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) is acidic and causes corrosion of indiumtin-oxide (ITO) anodes. Nickle oxide (NiO) are widely used as the hole transport layer (HTL) in QLED due to their suitable electrical properties. For the large energy gap between QD and HTL, there is unbalanced charge injection in QLED device when NiO is used. The energy band structures of NiO can be adjusted by Mg doping, which is an effective strategy to improve charge injection and mobility. Compared to undoped HIL, device with doped NiO give rise to higher EQE. In this work, our results suggests that Mg-doped NiO serve as a good hole injection layer materials for QLED and other optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: MIMO equalization for few-mode fiber transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, it is verified in experiments that 2X2 multiple-input multiple-output(MIMO) can implement mode demultiplexing in a mode division multiplexing (MDM) system. The Least Mean Square (LMS) algorithm and the Normalized LMS (NLMS) algorithm are applied to MIMO equalization, and the equalization performance of the NLMS is more stable under the same power.

articleTitle: WDM Optical Steganography Based on Super-Continuum Light Source
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a 10 Gb/s stealth channel based on super-continuum light source in 120km SSMF transmission system is experimented, which can be hidden under the public WDM channel in both time and frequency domain.

articleTitle: Five-port non-blocking silicon optical router based on mode-selective property
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a five-port optical router based on mode-selective property. It utilizes modes as labels to distinguish its routing paths. The optical signal-to-noise ratios for all paths are larger than 16.3 dB.

articleTitle: Anti-resonant reflecting effect in large-core hollow-core photonic crystal fiber for temperature sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical fiber sensors based on anti-resonant reflecting effect have attracted widespread attention in recent years. Here, a compact and robust all-fiber device is proposed and developed based on anti-resonant reflecting effect. A double-layered Fabry-Pérot resonator is built by infiltrating alcohol into two adjacent cladding holes of a new large-core hollow-core photonic crystal fiber. Due to the thermo-optic effect of alcohol, the temperature sensitivity of -0.184 nm/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C is achieved. This device can be good candidates in the field of physical or bio/chemical sensing.

articleTitle: Vector magnetic field sensor based on polarization-maintaining fiber long-period grating with magnetic fluid
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a vector magnetic field sensor based on long-period grating inscribed in thin-cladding polarization-maintaining fiber and immersed the grating in magnetic fluid. The proposed sensor can measure both magnetic intensity and orientation simultaneously.

articleTitle: Irreversible Photobleaching of BAC-Si in Bi/Er Co-Doped Optical Fiber under 830 nm Pumping
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The pump-induced bleaching effects upon luminescence of Bi/Er co-doped optical fiber (BEDF) have been investigated. The bismuth related luminescence is significantly bleached, especially BAC-Si, and can hardly recover to the initial level.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of System Parameters on Physical-Layer Security of Optical CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical CDMA (OCMDA) technology directly encrypts optical transmission links at the physical layer, which can improve the security of communication system against fibre-optic eavesdropping attacks. System parameters will affect the performances of OCDMA systems, based on the wiretap channel model of OCDMA systems, "secrecy capacity" is employed as an indicator to estimate the effects of system parameters (the type of code words, the length of code words) on the security of the systems. Simulation results demonstrate that system parameters play an important role and choosing the code words with better cross-correlation characteristics can improve the security of OCDMA systems.

articleTitle: 1.6 kW Raman fiber amplifier based on multimode graded index fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Power scaling of high power Raman fiber amplifier is demonstrated in this paper. The maximum output power reaches 1603.4W at 1130nm, which is the highest power achieved by Raman laser solely based on passive fiber.

articleTitle: Novel NOMA System for Optical Communications Based on OFDM/OQAM
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a NOMA-based OFDM/OQAM system theoretically in this paper. Our method outperformed conventional OFDM system on the total user throughput and spectral efficiency evidently. The proposal has been validated by theoretical derivation and numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: Simulation of analogue of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) based on metal metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the phenomenon of analogue of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) was theoretically realized using metal metamaterials based on periodic arrangement of one I-type cut wire (ICW) and two spiral ring resonators (SRRs). The EIT peak frequency is 0.598 THz and the Q value is about 18.16.

articleTitle: All-fiber Passively Mode-locked Femtosecond Laser Based on a Femtosecond Laser Inscribed 45° Tilted Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A femtosecond erbium-doped fiber laser using a novel 45° tilted fiber grating fabricated by direct femtosecond laser inscription is experimentally demonstrated. The laser generates stable short pulses with pulse width of 752 fs at 1562 nm.

articleTitle: Optical fiber temperature sensor based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated with a film of PDMS
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber temperature sensor by using a Mach-Zehner interferometer coated with a film of PDMS was proposed. The Mach-Zehner interferometer is made up of two Bowknot Type Tapers (BTTs) and a single mode fiber. The surface of the two BTTs was coated with a film of PDMS. The energy distribution of the two BTTs was simulated by using the finite element means. The proposed sensor structure has a linearity correlation of 98.46% in temperature responses. Temperature detection sensitivity of 0.1957nm/ °C was obtained under the temperature range from 40 °C to 120°C, which is about 10 times of the similar sensors with a sensitivity of tens pm/ °C.

articleTitle: Ultraviolet Micro Optical-Fiber Spectrometer Based on Linear array CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultraviolet micro optical-fiber spectrometer based on linear array CMOS is designed. The resolution is better than 0.1 nm in the range of 180-290nm. The wavelength error after calibration is less than 0.03 nm.

articleTitle: Low Noise Φ-OTDR Based on Frequency-Jitter-Free Heterodyne Demodulation Scheme
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a low noise Φ-OTDR is proposed which utilizes frequency-jitter-free heterodyne modulation scheme to retrieve the phase variations of Rayleigh backscattered light-waves along a sensing fiber. The heterodyne modulation scheme employs only one acousto-optic modulator (AOM), and thus is immune to the jitter of frequency shift of an AOM. Benefiting from that, the noise level of a Φ-OTDR is reduced. Multiple vibration events occurring simultaneously at different positions along the fiber are experimental restored by the proposed Φ-OTDR. The signal-to-noise ratio of 57.78 dB and the noise level as low as -65.4 dB (re 1rad/sqrt(Hz)) at 1 kHz are achieved.

articleTitle: Monolithic Linearly Polarized Nanosecond Fiber Laser with Record Peak Power and Near-Transform-Limited Linewidth
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiberized linearly polarized nanosecond fiber laser with high peak power and near-transfrom-limited linewidth is demonstrated based on master oscillator power amplifier structure. Employing the polarization-maintaining large-mode-area Yb-doped fiber with tapered longitudinal geometry, short length and high concentration, the main amplifier possesses excellent performance for nonlinear effect suppression, including stimulated Brillouin scattering effect and self-phase modulation effect. As a result, an average output power of 8.8 W with the pulse duration of 3.8 ns is obtained at the repetition frequency of 80 kHz after the amplification, corresponding to the peak power of ~30 kW and the pulse energy of 110 uJ. The near- transform-limited linewidth is maintained, accompanying high polarization extinction ratio of more than 16 dB and near-diffraction-limited beam quality with M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> factor of 1.2. It is known to be the record output power of all-fiber linearly polarized ns fiber laser with transform-limited linewidth, to the best of our knowledge.

articleTitle: Fiber-optic MZI activity monitoring based on RLS algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A non-invasive activity monitoring using Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is presented and recursive least square (RLS) algorithm is performed to classify presence and absence activity states with accuracy higher than 98.5% within 1 second.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Polar Code based on Gaussian Approximation for VLC system
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of polar codes constructed by Gaussian Approximation(GA) considering the characteristic of Visible Light Communication(VLC). The impact of key parameters in coding and decoding scheme is investigated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Low Polarization Dependent Loss Two-Dimensional Grating Coupler
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design and demonstrate a two-dimensional grating coupler (2D GC) with a low polarization dependent loss (PDL) based on the silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform. Using an elliptical-like etching pattern consisting of two identical semicircles and a rectangle embedded between them, a maximum PDL of the fabricated device is measured to be 0.2 dB covering the C-band, lower than that of most conventional 2D GCs. Besides, a large feature size of 280 nm is beneficial to its manufacturing process and wide application.

articleTitle: An in-fiber Acceleration Sensor based on Fabry–Perot Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact fiber-optic acceleration sensor based on Fabry-Perot interferometer is proposed and fabricated. The experimental results show that the minimum detectable acceleration of the accelerometer is 0.928 mg and the available bandwidth is 10-90 Hz.

articleTitle: Enhanced Adaptive DBP Using Extended Godard’s Error for 16-QAM Coherent Optical Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An enhanced adaptive digital backpropagation (A-DBP) scheme based on extended Godard's error is proposed and demonstrated experimentally for 16-quadrature amplitude (16QAM) modulation formats.

articleTitle: Single Core-offset Alignment for SFS Combs with High Extinction Ratio
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Alignment has a significant influence on the characteristics of single mode- few mode- single mode (SFS) fiber interferometer. In this paper, the fiber interferometer based on dual LP0n-mode few-mode fibers under single core-offset alignment is presented, which can provide a good comb spectrum. Compared with the axially aligned SFS, this alignment can obtain good extinction ratio using conventional fibers; compared with the both side core-offset SFS, this alignment can provide optimization fabrication and has good fabrication repeatability.

articleTitle: Characteristics of 1×2 Silicon Wavelength Selective Switch Using Arrayed - Waveguide Gratings with Fold-Back Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report characteristics of 200 GHz-spaced 20-channel 1 × 2 wavelength selective switch using single arrayed-waveguide grating with fold-back waveguides. The average insertion loss is 29.6 dB and the average extinction ratio is 10.9 dB.

articleTitle: Tunable Random Raman Fiber Laser at 1.7 μm Region with High Spectral Purity
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a cascaded random Raman fiber laser at 1715 μm with the record high purity of 98.29%. Furthermore, the wavelength tunability from 1705 to 1725 nm with spectral purity over 92% is achieved firstly.

articleTitle: Graphene enhanced intra-resonator biochemical detection with individual molecule sensitivity and selectivity
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Partially-reduced graphene oxide (prGO) inner-coated and fiber-calibrated Fabry-Perot dye resonator for biochemical detection enables the functionalized FRET-gain-assistance and intermode heterodyne interference, we achieve individual molecule sensitivity for dopamine, nicotine and ssDNA.

articleTitle: A Compact Adiabatic Silicon Photonic Edge Coupler Based on Silicon Nitride/Silicon Trident Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel compact adiabatic fiber-to-chip edge coupler based on a silicon nitride/silicon trident structure. The edge coupler can achieve high coupling efficiency up to 81% (namely 0.91 dB) with 3.2-μm lensed fiber in an ultra-broad bandwidth covering both the O-band and the C-band. It enables adiabatic mode conversion with a total length as short as 80 μm. The silicon nitride/silicon edge coupler is compatible with CMOS process and fabrication tolerance is also analysed for future fabrication and measurement.

articleTitle: Robust all polarization-maintaining femtosecond fiber laser with various phase bias
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a compact all polarization- maintaining mode-locked femtosecond fiber laser with three different non-reciprocal phase shifters. The achieved laser directly delivers 926 fs, 0.56 nJ pulses at the repetition rate of 88.3 MHz.

articleTitle: Optical-injection-seeded Optical Frequency Comb Generation Promoted by the Sub-harmonic Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and verify an optical-injection-seeded optical frequency comb generation scheme promoted by sub-harmonic modulation, wherein an optically injected semiconductor laser is driven into the nonlinear period-one oscillation state. An optical frequency combs with 17 comb lines is obtained in a flatness of 2.3dB. The tunability of the comb spacing and the change of the number of comb lines with the sub-harmonic modulation power are provided.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Shaping for Direct Detection Transmission With Kramers-Kronig Receiver
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We introduce probabilistic shaping into direct detection system with Kramers-Kronig receiver to further improve the performance. Simulation results show that there are 0.53/0.86/1.12dB OSNR improvements by transmitting PS-16/64/256QAM signal compared with the uniform 16/64/256QAM signal.

articleTitle: Two-way Optical Phase Comparison at 10-21 Level over 200-km fiber link
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This works demonstrates an improved local two-way optical phase comparison method. Based on this scheme, we implement a real-time frequency comparison over a bi-directional 200-km fiber spool link with a Bi-EDFA. The achieved relative frequency stability is 9.7E-18 at 1 s integration time and reaches 1.4E-21 at 10,000 s.

articleTitle: Industry Trends for 400 Gb/s and Beyond Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: After the implementation of 100-Gb/s pluggable optics, the optical communications industry is marching towards 400-Gb/s era. We will review our recent demonstration and study for 400 Gb/s and beyond client and line side optical interconnect.

articleTitle: Characterization of a MOPA system used for underwater optical communication
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Underwater water optical communication (UWOC) requires high-power laser transmitter with good beam quality for high-rate data modulation. Since master oscillator power amplifier (MOPA) has the characteristic of preserving the property of seed laser (e.g. bandwidth and beam quality), it is expected to resolve the problem. In this paper, we theoretically simulate the large-signal modeling of the amplified laser light and the frequency response of a MOPA system and experimentally amplified 3-mW 1-um light to 145mW. The seed light came from 1064-nm TO-Packaged laser diode and was coupled into HI1060. To satisfy the requirements of the transmitters for UWOC, we used second harmonic generation and got 0.06mW 532-nm laser light. Finally, according to the theoretical analysis of a MOPA system and the electrical response of a laser driver, we chose Manchester Encoding to modulate the amplified 1064-nm laser light and achieved 100-Mbps transmission. The system was error free for 1◊10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> bits.

articleTitle: An Improved FPGA Parallel Design of Frequency Offset Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In coherent optical communication QPSK system, an improved FPGA parallel design of frequency offset estimation with low complexity is proposed. The BER simulation results compared with serial scheme verify the feasibility of the parallel design.

articleTitle: Compensation of Laser Phase Noise Based on Polar-Coordinates Decision
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we proposed and experimentally demonstrated a phase-noise-mitigation scheme based on polar coordinates decision in the 16-QAM coherent optical communication system. The BER curves are measured to verify the feasibility of the scheme.

articleTitle: Cluster Synchronization of Semiconductor Lasers Network with Heterogeneous Coupling Delays
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The cluster synchronization of mutually coupled semiconductor lasers network with heterogeneous delays is systematically investigated, whose applicability is demonstrated by discussing two simple networks and a random network with Gaussian-distribution heterogeneous coupling delays.

articleTitle: Design of Suspended Sub-wavelength Terahertz Waveguide Connector
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The design of a sub-wavelength terahertz waveguide in presented. The high transmission efficiency of the waveguide and the good coupling between the components are demonstrated by using finite element method and beam propagation method.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation by dual-pulse-pumping in photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and numerically investigate a scheme of supercontinuum generation from photonic crystal fibers using dual-pulse-pumping at 1064nm. The pumping source is united by a femtosecond pulse and a picosecond pulse with the same peak power 3000W. Our simulation results indicate this pump way can make good use of fiber as long as the offset time is small enough. In the normal dispersion region, other nonlinear effects have broadened the spectra before four-wave mixing. Just shorter than 1m fiber will be required to extend spectrum from signal wavelength to idler wavelength in the case that no offset time existed.

articleTitle: Surface modification of CdSe/CdS/ZnS quantum dots with mercapto acid
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The surface ligands of the quantum dots (QDs) play an important role in the performance of quantum dots based optoelectronic devices. However, the native surface ligands of long-chain non-polar aliphatic compounds are hydrophobic, which limits the application of QDs for further device fabrication. Here, we reported a simple and fast method for cap exchange of CdSe/CdS/ZnS quantum dots using thiol functional ligands. We can successfully transfer QDs from non-polar to polar solvents by utilizing this facile method without significant fluorescence quenching.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wide-Spectral Mode-Locking Fiber Laser Carriers in Free Space Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an optimization of wide-spectral mode-locking fiber laser carriers by the introduction of two-pulse pump scheme with fiber dispersion management. We also verify the improved transmission performance of optimized wider-spectral carriers in 1km simulated atmospheric turbulent channel. For preferable compatibility and superiority, it can be an adaptive scheme for free space optical communication in the foreseeable future.

articleTitle: A Unified Form of Common Model Predictive Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In view of the various forms of model predictive control (MPC) algorithms, it brings inconveniences such as the need to build a complete simulation environment when carrying out simulation experiments under different requirements of different occasions. This paper establishes a unified mathematical form for common predictive control, which provides conditions for building a unified forecasting control algorithm simulation platform and other requirements.

articleTitle: A Novel Optimized PTS for PAPR reduction of an DMT signal
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Partial Transmit Sequence (PTS) algorithm can effectively reduce the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of the Discrete Multi-Tone Modulation (DMT) signal, but it is difficult to apply in practical operation like short-distance scene because of its high complexity. Based on the PTS technique, Progressive-Segmented PTS (PS-PTS) and its improved algorithm named IPS-PTS are proposed. We carried out simulation experiments under DMT modulation format and Gaussian white noise channel. The results show that the proposed algorithms can effectively reduce the PAPR of signal and get a balance between performance and computational complexity.

articleTitle: The application of PCA on Փ-OTDR sensing system for vibration detection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The paper presents Principal Component Analysis (PCA) technique in denoising phase sensitive optical time domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) sensing data for vibration detection. The PCA is one of the most effective techniques used for noise reduction while preserving significant details of the denoised signals. As a result, we outline the basics of PCA and applied on the said data. It demonstrates that the PCA significantly reduced the noise and vibration along the phase trace clearly detected with a significant enhancement of the Signal to Noise ratio (SNR). A theoretical analysis is presented with an experimental demonstration of the vibration sensing range of 1km and a spatial resolution of 10m.

Author Keywords: Phase Sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometry

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental study on optical fiber microseismic accelerometer based on cantilever beam structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: According to the characteristics of underground environment and microseismic signal in coal mine, a kind of optical fiber microseismic accelerometer based on cantilever beam structure is put forward in this paper, and its mechanical model is established, its sensitivity is analyzed, and tested by B&K shaking table test system. The experimental results show that the frequency response range of the sensor is 10Hz-100Hz, which meets the requirements of microseismic test..

articleTitle: Humidity and temperature sensor based on pokal-taper and lateral-offset structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An interferometric optical fiber sensor based on pokal-taper structure and lateral-offset structure is proposed. In order to increase the humidity sensitivity of the sensor, the sensing area is coated with 1mg/ml concentration of graphene dispersion. The temperature sensitivities are 0.097nm/°C and 0.127nm/°C in the temperature range of 0°C~40°C. The humidity sensitivities are 0.039nm/%RH and 0.042nm/%RH in the humidity range of 30%~70%. With some advantages of small size, anti-electromagnetic interference, the proposed sensor has broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Investigations on FM-to-AM modulation compensation using all-fibered wide-range tunable filter
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fibered wide-range tunable filter to compensate the frequency modulation to amplitude modulation (FM-to-AM) conversion in laser driver facility is investigated and demonstrated. The filter is based on polarization interference technology and the numerical model referred to Jones matrix method is developed. In the demonstrated compensation experiment, FM-to-AM index α is reduced from 16.78% to 3.12%.

articleTitle: In-fiber Surface Plasmon Resonance Temperature Sensor Based on PDMS Infiltrated Hollow Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An in-fiber surface plasmon resonance temperature sensor based on Polydimethylsiloxane infiltrated hollow core fiber was proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Results demonstrated that the proposed sensor behaved high sensitivity of -1.05nm/℃, small size, and good stability.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensor Based on Mach-Zehnder Interferometer with Corroded Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A temperature sensor by using a corroded photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. It is fabricated by sandwiching a corroded PCF between two standard single mode fibers (SMFs) with the original region of the air holes of the PCF transforming into a hexagonal ring air cavity. The proposed sensor is linearly responsive to temperature within the range from 25°C to 100°C, with the sensitivity of 2.9 pm/°C, which makes it a highly promising for practical high temperature monitoring application.

articleTitle: The high-temperature stability of fiber Bragg gratings fabricated by 193 nm excimer laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have demonstrated the fiber Bragg gratings (FBG) fabricated on different fibres by using the excimer laser (193 nm) and phase mask. The FBG is annealed at 400 °C for 70 days. The wavelength shift of FBG at 400 °C has been investigated. After the FBG is annealed for a long time, the wavelength shift of the FBG approaches stability. Then, the relationship between wavelength shift of FBG and annealing time has been obtained.

articleTitle: Design of a current modulation driver for an ultra-compact RGB laser
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: RGB lasers have been widely used as light sources in projectors, endoscopes, HUD(Head up Displays) and many other displays. In this study, we designed a current driver circuit for an ultra-compact RGB laser, which allows for high speed driving current modulations. This characteristic is suitable for scanning display in many occasions. The laser current driver circuit is consisted of the current driver and the temperature controller. The current driver has three independently high-speed current modulation channels. We have tested the P-I performance of the RGB laser and the highest current modulation speed is 1.55 MHz.

articleTitle: Clock Recovery Based on Adaptive Phase Error Detection for Coherent Optical Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Traditional clock recovery techniques rely on Gardner for phase error detection to recover the original signal. An adaptive phase splitting detection technique is proposed by joint channel equalization in this paper. The loop judges the current error by the error of the previous moment, reduces the phase error jitter, and improves the stability of the system. In addition, the algorithm works well for the same phase of adjacent symbols through phase splitting techniques. In fiber channel, this scheme is more suitable for the case of small roll-off factor (ROF). Simulation results show that the algorithm is suitable for signals modulated by MQAM. The algorithm performs very well even when the ROF approaches 0.

articleTitle: Signal and noise analysis in resonant photoacoustic spectroscopy using fast Fourier transform
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple method based on fast Fourier transform (FFT) is used to analyze the signal and noise in resonant photoacoustic spectroscopy. Varying the sampling time, the photoacoustic signal and noise are analyzed using FFT method, and compared with lock-in amplifier method. A detection limit of 1 ppm of methane has been achieved in pure nitrogen using a 1653 nm laser with an average power of 3.6 mW.

articleTitle: Twin tunable laser system with wavelength calibration for Tera-Hertz spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, a laser beat system based on two DBR tunable lasers was bulid. The laser output wavelength is calibrated by the wavelength calibration device, in order to get the precise beat frequency. Finaly, we demonstrated a Tera-Hertz spectrometer using this two laser beat light source. This beat laser system has the advantages of low-cost, easy access, and fast wavelength tuning.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Network Behavior Feature Detection Model Based on Knowledge Base
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the rapid increase of network information, the problem of network security has become increasingly prominent. Monitoring the specific online behavior of target groups is a measure to prevent network security awareness. In this paper, a network user behavior monitoring model based on knowledge base is proposed. This model combines fast multi-pattern matching technology, which can match the existing behavior features in the knowledge base quickly, efficiently and accurately in the network environment with large traffic. Its advantage is that the feature knowledge base can be flexibly extended and controlled. This model not only facilitates the management of managers, but also monitors the specific behavior of network users in high-speed network environment.

articleTitle: Femtosecnod Laser Ablated Fiber SERS-DNA Probe and Applications in Deafness Gene Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a fiber SERS-DNA probe was fabricated with femtosecond laser ablation and laser-induced silver particle deposition, and a single DNA strand with a stem-ring molecular beacon was modified onto the probe. Deafness gene was detected in the target solution by monitoring the SERS signal intensity of the molecular beacon. The experimental results showed that low DNA concentration down to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> M could be successfully detected with such a fiber SERS-DNA probe, which shows an alternative method for the detection of virulence gene.

articleTitle: High-efficiency soluble thermally activated delayed fluorescent OLED with multilayer hole transport layers
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Solution processed organic light emitting devices (OLEDs) incorporating a soluble thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF) emitter were fabricated with three hole-transport layers (HTL), poly(N-vinylcarbazole) (PVK), poly(9,9-dioctylfluorene-alt-N-(4-sec-butylphenyl)-diphenylamine) (TFB), and TFB/PVK as the multilayer HTL. The device with multilayer HTLs demonstrated the highest external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 6.9%, the lowest driving voltage of 4.8V, and the highest luminance.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized Airy beam generation with hyperbolic metamaterials at telecom wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Metasurfaces have shown great promise for generation of Airy beams, but the available plasmonic/dielectric metasurfaces based circularly polarized Airy beam generators suffer from low efficiency and/or lack of amplitude modulation. Hyperbolic metamaterials (HMMs) have shown great potential to modulate electromagnetic waves with high efficiency in multiple dimensions, including amplitude, phase and polarization. Here, we propose to use HMM waveguide array to generate circularly polarized Airy beam at telecom wavelengths with both phase and amplitude modulation, and verify the excellent performance with simulation. Our strategy may offer a general approach to generate complicated electromagnetic fields with the requirement of varying amplitudes and phases simultaneously.

articleTitle: Quasi-Tamm Plasmon Polaritons in metal-dielectric-metal waveguide and its sensing application
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel metal-dielectric-metal waveguide structure is designed, where a novel type of Tamm states called quasi-Tamm plasmon polaritons emerge and exhibit an efficient local field enhancement. Furthermore, its sensing application is analyzed.

articleTitle: Strain Sensor Based on Mach-Zehnder Interferometers by Waist-enlarged Structure and Spherical Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical fiber sensors based on waist-enlarged structure and spherical structure were proposed for strain measurement. Their fabrication process and experimental results were compared. The strain sensitivities of the sensors based on the waist-enlarged structure and the spherical structure are -0.66pm/με and -1.28pm/με, respectively. It shows that the Mach-Zehnder sensor fabricated by the waist-enlarged structure has the advantages of good repeatability and easy fabrication, and the Mach-Zehnder sensor based on the spherical structure has higher sensitivity for strain measurement.

articleTitle: Hybrid Plasmonic Waveguide based 3×3 Multimode Interferometer for Compact 120° Optical Hybrid
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on hybrid plasmonic waveguide (HPW), we propose a compact 3×3 multimode interferometer (MMI) for 120° optical hybrid. Also, tapered HPW sections are implemented to improve the coupling efficiencies for lights coupled into/out of the multimode section. The simulation results show that at a wavelength of 1550 nm, the transmission rate of the 3×3 HPW-MMI is 0.692 (1.61 dB loss), the maximum transmission imbalance is 0.43 dB, and the phase error is 4.66°.

articleTitle: Raman Dissipative-soliton Generation with a Nonlinear Optical Loop Mirror in a Polarization Maintaining Fiber Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a Raman dissipative soliton generated in a mode-locked fiber laser with a nonlinear optical loop mirror. This configuration provides a method to obtain linearly polarized ultrafast laser at flexible wavelengths.

articleTitle: Wide-spectrum properties of Yb: YAG crystal-derived fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We designed and fabricated an Yb: YAG crystal-derived fiber (YDF) by CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-laser drawing tower. The fluorescence spectra and amplifier characteristics were discussed in detail.

articleTitle: More-than-95-line fiber laser based on hybrid gain from the Brillouin effect and erbium-doped fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a multi-wavelength Brillouin fiber laser based on a dual-ring structure to take advantage of the forward and backward Brillouin gain simultaneously with an injected tunable scanning lasing. We used two erbium-doped fiber amplifiers for the amplification of the seed lasing and the operated Brillouin laser. The cascaded stimulated Brillouin effect in the section of dispersion-shifted fiber contributes to the free-oscillation suppression in cavity. When the laser operates at the center wavelength of 1565 nm, the output spectra shows the maximum Brillouin lines of more than 95 with a wavelength spacing of about 0.08 nm under the maximum pump. Through adjusting of the seed wavelength and the tunable filter in cavity, the output spectra can be shifted from 1540 to 1570 nm.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive Liquid-Level Modal Sensor Utilizing Thin-Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical modal interferometer based on thin-core fiber (TCF) for liquid-level sensing is proposed and demonstrated. Experimental results show that the wavelength shift sensitivity is -0.124 nm/mm within the measurement range of 15mm.

articleTitle: Research on the resonance frequency reduction of the single fiber scanner
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Single fiber scanner has been applied in many fields, such as minimally invasive surgery, nondestructive testing(NDT), borescopy technology. The resonance frequency of the single fiber cantilever is an important parameter for a scanner. Especially in the application of OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography), a relatively low resonance frequency is required. In this study, we proposed a new method to lower the resonance frequency of the single fiber scanner, other than simply lengthening the fiber. The simulation results agree well with the measured data.

articleTitle: Embedding Hose-Model virtual Network in Flexgrid Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This work studies the problem of hose-model virtual network embedding in flexgrid optical networks. Problem definition is given, and four heuristic algorithms are proposed. Their performance is assessed under different traffic loads by simulation.

articleTitle: Designing of Surface Plasmon Sensor in a Side Hole Fiber with Simultaneous Double Channel Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor with high sensitivity and symmetrical double channel is proposed. A side hole fiber has been considered as a platform of the proposed sensor. Detailed numerical calculation is carried out with the full-vector finite-element method. A polarization-maintaining single mode fiber considered for the simulation purposes two symmetrical holes introduced in the boundary of the core-cladding interface for dual-channel detection purpose. Metal layers are introduced in the inner wall of the hole. Numerically computed results show that the sensor can work in the range of different refractive index (RI) from 1.30 to 1.43. Sensitivity can be reached as high as 8800nm/RIU around 1.43. The average sensitivity of the developed sensors is 5160nm/RIU is obtained.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation from PCF directly pumped by DSR laser with kW-level peak power
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed and experimentally demonstrated an all-fiber supercontinuum (SC) source with pump power independent spectral distribution by directly pumping dissipative soliton resonance (DSR) pulses with kW-level peak power into photonics crystal fiber (PCF).

articleTitle: Effect of gold coating on distributed strain measurement at high temperature up to 700°C by DPP-BOTDA
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, we thoroughly investigate the effect of the gold coating of Gold-coated fiber (GCF) on strain measurement at high temperature up to 700 °C with differential pulse pair Brillouin optical time analysis (DPP-BOTDA). Owing to the residual stress that solidified in the GCF during the cooling process of coating, the GCF would first undergo plastic deformation and then elastic deformation in the strain measurement. After one-time strain measurement to remove the residual stress of GCF, the maximum standard deviations of the strain coefficients at high-temperature is ±1.3%, which is mainly due to the non-uniform thickness of the gold coating and the nonuniformity of silica fiber at high temperature.

articleTitle: An Optical Communication System Adjusting Method for GEO Satellites
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an optical communication system adjusting method for the geostationary-earth-orbit (GEO) satellites. The proposal is demonstrated and evaluated by theoretical analysis and experiments. It is able to guarantee not only the coherent detection communications among the GEO satellites but also the direct detection communications between the GEO satellite and the low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite.

articleTitle: Amplification of surface plasmons on a staggered doubly-corrugated metallic surfaces by electron beam
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Surface plasmon polaritons(SPP) is a special bounded optical surface wave and can find many novel applications such as imaging, sensing, optical communications, etc. In this paper, the theoretical and numerical studies on the excitation of surface plasmon modes on a symmetric doubly-corrugated metallic surface with a staggered distance by electron beam are presented. According to the matched wave momentum of SPP mode and electron beam, SPP mode can be excited and amplified along corrugated metallic waveguide by injected electron beam within an operation frequency band. Besides, the numerical results of the interaction of SSP mode and electron beam on the structure based on a FDTD algorithm are given in terahertz band. The presented studies about the novel excitation method of SPP mode on the staggered doublycorrugated metallic gratings by electron beam can open up new ways to develop some novel optoelectronic and plasmonic devices such as integrated waveguide, filters and enhanced terahertz radiation source.

articleTitle: CO2-laser written helical long-period gratings with resonance at second-order diffraction
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate the fabrication of helical long-period gratings (HLPGs) with resonance at second-order diffraction for the first time. The torsion, temperature and bending sensing characteristics are investigated experimentally.

articleTitle: First Principles study of nanostructured VS2 electrodes for Na-ion batteries
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The dynamic structural evolution and reaction kinetics of VS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-based nanosheets as anode materials for NIBs was reported by using DFT calculations. The 2H VS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> phase is favourable for sodium adsorption than the 1T VS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> phase.

articleTitle: Phase Noise Estimation for Nonlinear Frequency Division Multiplexing System
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For nonlinear frequency division multiplexing system, a transmission model in the presence of phase noise was derived, and a blind phase noise estimation method based on decision directed free technology was exploited and verified.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Expression of Bit Error Rate of PCM-FM using Non-coherent Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: PCM/FM, also known as CPFSK, is widely used in aeronautical telemetry. However, there is still no theoretical expression of its bit error rate in the literature. In this paper, based on the analysis of non-coherent detection of PCM/FM signal, a mathematical expression is derived. The analytical result is verified by computer simulation and compared with other modulation schemes and the proposed expression can significantly benefit the system design and evaluation of receiver performance.

articleTitle: Broadband Optical Router Based on Photonic-plasmonic Hybrid Switches
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical router is the key element for Optical Network-on-chip (ONoC). Here we propose Zander, a five-port non-blocking broadband optical router based on photonic-plasmonic hybrid switches. Furthermore, Zander-XY is proposed for XY dimension-order routing.

articleTitle: Three-Stage Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation Based On Fairness in Software-Defined Hybrid Passive Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Software-defined hybrid passive optical network (HPON) is an intelligent architecture and can implement the coexistence of multiple PON systems using various physical layer (PHY) multiplexing technologies. By introducing the concept of virtual PON (VPON), a three-stage dynamic bandwidth allocation algorithm based on fairness for original and new VPONs in software-defined HPON is proposed. The performance benefits of the proposed algorithm in terms of bandwidth utilization, access probability of new VPONs and fairness index are verified through network simulation.

articleTitle: Multimode waveguide Bragg gratings on SOI platform
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Multimode waveguide Bragg gratings (MWBGs) are demonstrated on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform for on-chip applications, such as band-pass and band-rejection filter, add-drop filter, polarization beam splitter and mode multi/demultiplexers. The operating principle is based on the contra-directional coupling between the fundamental transverse electric mode and different higher-order modes, which depends on the symmetry or the asymmetry properties of the periodic refractive-index perturbations. The designs and experimental results of different MWBGs based devices are presented.

articleTitle: Overhead Transmission Line Tensiometer on Insulator String Based on Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes an overhead transmission line tensiometer on insulator string based on fiber Bragg grating and cantilever beam. According to the simulation and experiment, the tensiometer is suitable for overhead transmission line breakage warning.

articleTitle: High speed secure optical communication based on optical code processing (Invited paper)
publicationTitle: 2019 18th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we review the recent advances and demonstrations of time domain pseudorandom optical phase encoding technology for high speed 40Gb/s OOK and DPSK secure optical communication systems. Bit-by-bit code shifting technique for enhancing the information security is proposed and demonstrated in different optical transmission systems with various bit rates and modulation formats. The potential application of the proposed techniques for high speed secure optical transmission systems is envisioned.
